cards.statement: In stress testing, a static balance sheet assumption is more conservative in all cases, since it prevents the bank from assuming any mitigating action.
cards.explanation: Neither balance sheet assumption is unambiguously conservative. A static balance sheet can, for example, understate RWA migration as credit quality deteriorates.
cards.originalText: A static assumption is more conservative in all cases, since it prevents the bank from assuming any mitigating action.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: A strong risk identification practice within a bank holding company's capital adequacy process is comprehensive, firm-wide and regularly refreshed, covers all exposures and activities, explicitly reaches risks not well captured by the supervisory scenario, assigns an owner to each identified risk, and documents a link from each material risk to the loss estimation methodology that captures it.
cards.explanation: Under Principle 1, identification must cover all material risks, including those the supervisory scenario misses, because a risk never identified is never estimated or capitalised. Each material risk should be traceable to a loss estimation method.
cards.originalText: A comprehensive, firm-wide and regularly refreshed identification process covering all exposures and activities, explicitly reaching risks not well captured by the supervisory scenario, with an owner for each identified risk and a documented link from each material risk to the loss estimation methodology that captures it.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: Scoping risk identification to the variables contained in the supervisory scenario is a strong practice within a bank holding company's capital adequacy process, so that identification and estimation are aligned.
cards.explanation: Scoping risk identification to the supervisory scenario guarantees blindness to idiosyncratic risks the supervisor did not model. Identification must be comprehensive and firm-wide.
cards.originalText: A risk identification exercise scoped to the variables contained in the supervisory scenario, so that identification and estimation are aligned.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: Performing risk identification once at the inception of the capital planning framework, and thereafter updating it only when the business acquires a new legal entity, is a strong practice within a bank holding company's capital adequacy process.
cards.explanation: Risk identification must be refreshed regularly, because new products, changing concentrations and evolving markets alter the risk inventory without any change in legal entities.
cards.originalText: A risk identification exercise performed once at the inception of the capital planning framework and thereafter updated only when the business acquires a new legal entity.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: Risk identification within a bank holding company's capital adequacy process should be owned exclusively by the independent risk function, so that business line optimism does not influence the inventory.
cards.explanation: Exclusive ownership by the risk function removes the business knowledge that identification depends on. The business identifies its risks, while the risk function facilitates and challenges.
cards.originalText: A risk identification process owned exclusively by the independent risk function, so that business line optimism does not influence the inventory.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: Supervisory expectations for internal controls and governance over a bank holding company's capital adequacy process include independent model review and validation covering the models used in capital planning; documented policies and procedures with change control; comprehensive documentation sufficient for an independent party to reproduce the results; internal audit review of the process; and board oversight extending to periodic review of the risk infrastructure and estimation methodologies, evaluation of capital goals, assessment of scenario appropriateness, and approval of capital decisions.
cards.explanation: Principles 6 and 7 wrap the capital adequacy process in internal controls and governance. Board oversight extends beyond approving the final plan to methodologies, capital goals, scenario appropriateness and capital decisions.
cards.originalText: Independent model review and validation covering the models used in capital planning; documented policies and procedures with change control; comprehensive documentation sufficient for an independent party to reproduce the results; internal audit review of the process; and board oversight extending to periodic review of the risk infrastructure and estimation methodologies, evaluation of capital goals, assessment of scenario appropriateness, and approval of capital decisions.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: In a bank holding company's capital adequacy process, the board need only approve the final capital plan, with the underlying methodology, assumptions and limitations reviewed at management level only, so that board time is used efficiently.
cards.explanation: Board oversight of the capital adequacy process expressly extends to methodologies, assumptions, limitations and scenario appropriateness, not just approval of the final plan.
cards.originalText: Board approval of the final capital plan, with the underlying methodology, assumptions and limitations reviewed at management level only, so that board time is used efficiently.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: Capital planning models should be validated by the teams that built them, since capital planning models are too specialised for an independent function to review.
cards.explanation: Independent model review and validation is a named component of the capital adequacy process controls (Principle 6), and specialisation is never a reason to abandon independence.
cards.originalText: Validation of capital planning models by the teams that built them, since capital planning models are too specialised for an independent function to review.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: Documentation for a bank holding company's capital adequacy process need only be sufficient for the bank's own staff to reproduce the results, with external reproducibility unnecessary given the proprietary nature of the methodology.
cards.explanation: Capital planning documentation must allow an independent party to reproduce the results, which is what makes audit, validation and supervisory review possible.
cards.originalText: Documentation sufficient for the bank's own staff to reproduce the results, with external reproducibility unnecessary given the proprietary nature of the methodology.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: A strong capital policy at a bank holding company states capital goals and targets with the analysis supporting them, sets out how capital actions such as dividends, repurchases and issuance are determined in a range of conditions, and contains a capital contingency plan specifying the triggers and the actions to be taken if capital approaches or falls below target.
cards.explanation: Under Principle 5, a capital policy sets out goals and targets with supporting analysis, a framework for capital actions such as dividends, buybacks and issuance across conditions, and a contingency plan with triggers and pre-agreed actions.
cards.originalText: A policy stating capital goals and targets with the analysis supporting them, setting out how capital actions such as dividends, repurchases and issuance are determined in a range of conditions, and containing a capital contingency plan specifying the triggers and the actions to be taken if capital approaches or falls below target.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: A strong capital policy at a bank holding company sets a single minimum capital ratio equal to the regulatory minimum, since holding capital above the minimum destroys shareholder value.
cards.explanation: A capital target set at the regulatory minimum guarantees a breach on any adverse move. Capital buffers are designed to be drawn down in stress.
cards.originalText: A policy setting a single minimum capital ratio equal to the regulatory minimum, since holding capital above the minimum destroys shareholder value.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: A strong capital policy at a bank holding company specifies a target dividend payout ratio to be maintained irrespective of conditions, so that shareholders receive a predictable return.
cards.explanation: Distributions must be conditional on capital adequacy under stress. A payout ratio maintained regardless of conditions contradicts the purpose of a capital policy.
cards.originalText: A policy specifying a target dividend payout ratio to be maintained irrespective of conditions, so that shareholders receive a predictable return.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.loText: Describe practices that can result in a strong and effective capital adequacy process for a BHC in the following areas: - Risk identification - Internal controls, including model review and validation - Corporate governance - Capital policy, including setting of goals and targets and contingency planning - Stress testing and stress scenario design - Estimating losses, revenues, and expenses, including quantitative and qualitative methodologies - Assessing the impact of capital adequacy, including risk-weighted asset (RWA) and balance sheet projections
cards.reading: ORR-20: Capital Planning at Large Bank Holding Companies
cards.statement: A strong capital policy at a bank holding company defers all capital action decisions to the point at which they arise, since pre-committing to contingent actions removes management flexibility.
cards.explanation: Capital contingency planning exists because decisions taken under stress are worse and more constrained than those agreed in advance, so a strong policy pre-commits triggers and actions.
cards.originalText: A policy deferring all capital action decisions to the point at which they arise, since pre-committing to contingent actions removes management flexibility.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Data entry errors and incomplete legal documentation fall under the Basel level 1 category execution, delivery, and process management.
cards.explanation: Processing errors and missing or incomplete documentation are standard examples of execution, delivery, and process management (EDPM).
cards.originalText: Data entry errors and incomplete legal documentation fall under execution, delivery, and process management.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Internal fraud and external fraud belong to the same Basel level 1 event risk category.
cards.explanation: Internal fraud and external fraud are two separate level 1 categories; the split is by perpetrator, an employee versus an outsider.
cards.originalText: Internal fraud and external fraud belong to the same event risk category.
cards.correction: Internal fraud and external fraud belong to different Basel level 1 event risk categories.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Losses from theft and hacking are examples of the Basel level 1 category damage to physical assets.
cards.explanation: Theft and hacking by outsiders are external fraud. Damage to physical assets covers physical destruction such as natural disasters or destruction of equipment.
cards.originalText: Losses from theft and hacking are examples of the damage to physical assets category.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Vendor disputes are an example of the Basel level 1 event type execution, delivery, and process management.
cards.explanation: Disputes with vendors and trade counterparties arise from failed process management, so they sit in execution, delivery, and process management (EDPM).
cards.originalText: Vendor disputes

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Destruction of equipment is an example of the Basel level 1 event type execution, delivery, and process management.
cards.explanation: Destruction of equipment is an example of damage to physical assets (DPA), not a process failure.
cards.originalText: Destruction of equipment
cards.correction: Destruction of equipment is an example of the Basel level 1 event type damage to physical assets.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Employment contract termination is an example of the Basel level 1 event type execution, delivery, and process management.
cards.explanation: Employment contract termination issues are an example of employment practices and workplace safety (EPWS).
cards.originalText: Employment contract termination
cards.correction: Employment contract termination is an example of the Basel level 1 event type employment practices and workplace safety.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The Basel level 1 event type employment practices and workplace safety covers losses from acts inconsistent with employment, health or safety laws and from diversity and discrimination events.
cards.explanation: Employment practices and workplace safety (EPWS) captures losses from breaches of employment law, workplace safety failures and discrimination.
cards.originalText: Employment practices and workplace safety

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The Basel level 1 event type clients, products, and business practices covers losses from acts inconsistent with employment, health or safety laws and from diversity and discrimination events.
cards.explanation: Those workforce-related losses belong to employment practices and workplace safety. Clients, products, and business practices covers client misinformation, product errors and regulatory fines.
cards.originalText: Clients, products, and business practices
cards.correction: The Basel level 1 event type employment practices and workplace safety covers losses from acts inconsistent with employment, health or safety laws and from diversity and discrimination events.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Legal-risk losses are excluded from the Basel level 1 loss mapping because they cannot be cleanly mapped to any single level 1 category.
cards.explanation: The Basel definition of operational risk includes legal risk, so legal losses are not excluded from the mapping.
cards.originalText: She excluded legal‑risk losses because they cannot be cleanly mapped to any single level 1 category.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: External fraud is a high-frequency Basel level 1 category that is heterogeneous, containing both low-severity and high-severity events.
cards.explanation: In industry (ORX) data external fraud is about 30% of loss frequency but only about 9% of severity: many small card frauds coexist with rare, severe hacking events.
cards.originalText: External fraud is high‑frequency but heterogeneous, containing both low‑severity and high‑severity events.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: In industry loss data, the largest share of operational loss severity falls in the Basel level 1 category clients, products, and business practices.
cards.explanation: Clients, products, and business practices accounts for about 52% of severity, driven by large regulatory fines and client compensation.
cards.originalText: In terms of severity, the largest losses accrue to the clients, products, and business practices (CPBP) category.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Damage to physical assets tends to produce among the least severe operational losses and has among the lowest frequencies of the Basel level 1 categories.
cards.explanation: In industry data damage to physical assets accounts for only about 1% of both frequency and severity.
cards.originalText: Damage to physical assets (DPA) tends to produce among the least severe losses and has among the lowest frequencies.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Losses caused by defective software or IT system failures are assigned to the Basel level 1 event type business disruption and system failures.
cards.explanation: Software and IT system failures, such as breakdowns and outages, are the core of business disruption and system failures (BDSF).
cards.originalText: Business disruption and system failures

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Clients, products, and business practices is the Basel level 1 event category that most likely produces the greatest loss severity for a financial institution.
cards.explanation: It accounts for over half of total loss severity in industry data because of large regulatory fines and client compensation.
cards.originalText: Client, products, and business practices (CPBP).

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: External fraud is the Basel level 1 event category that most likely produces the greatest loss severity for a financial institution.
cards.explanation: External fraud is high frequency but only about 9% of severity. Clients, products, and business practices produces the greatest severity.
cards.originalText: External fraud (EF).
cards.correction: Clients, products, and business practices is the Basel level 1 event category that most likely produces the greatest loss severity for a financial institution.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Execution, delivery, and process management is the Basel level 1 event category covering losses from failed transaction processing and from relations with trade counterparties and vendors.
cards.explanation: EDPM covers failures to process transactions and manage processes, including vendor and counterparty disputes.
cards.originalText: Execution, delivery, and process management

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Internal fraud is the Basel level 1 event category covering losses from failed transaction processing and from relations with trade counterparties and vendors.
cards.explanation: Internal fraud involves intentional misconduct by employees. Failed processing and vendor or counterparty relations belong to execution, delivery, and process management.
cards.originalText: Internal fraud
cards.correction: Execution, delivery, and process management is the Basel level 1 event category covering losses from failed transaction processing and from relations with trade counterparties and vendors.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: A loss caused by back-office confusion that delays settlement of a trade with a counterparty is assigned to the Basel level 1 category execution, delivery, and process management.
cards.explanation: Late settlement caused by a back-office process failure toward a trade counterparty is a classic example of execution, delivery, and process management.
cards.originalText: Execution, Delivery, and Process Management

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Improper business or market practices is a Basel level 1 event risk category.
cards.explanation: Improper business or market practices is a level 2 sub-category under the level 1 category clients, products, and business practices.
cards.originalText: Improper Business or Market Practices
cards.correction: Improper business or market practices is a Basel level 2 category under clients, products, and business practices.

changes.to: level 2 category under clients, products, and business practices

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe the seven Basel II event risk categories and identify examples of operational risk events in each category.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: A client lawsuit alleging that an advisor put commission and firm profit ahead of the client's best interest, a fiduciary breach, is assigned to the Basel level 1 category clients, products, and business practices.
cards.explanation: Failure to meet a professional obligation to clients, such as a fiduciary or suitability duty, falls under clients, products, and business practices (CPBP).
cards.originalText: Clients, Products, and Business Practices

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: In the UK regulators' description of operational resilience, important business services mark the shift from a process-based view of continuity to a service-based view.
cards.explanation: Important business services identify the services whose disruption would cause intolerable harm to consumers or market integrity, replacing the process-by-process view.
cards.originalText: Important business services: From a process‑based view of continuity, the regulator moved to a service‑based view to ensure continuity

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: In the UK regulators' description of operational resilience, the continuity of business services component requires firms to respond to disruptions, maintain trust among key stakeholders and communicate clearly during a crisis.
cards.explanation: Responding to disruptions, maintaining stakeholder trust and communicating clearly describe the management of disruption component, not continuity of business services.
cards.originalText: Continuity of business services: To contribute to the stability of the system, firms should respond to disruptions, maintain trust among key stakeholders, and provide clarity of communication during a crisis
cards.correction: In the UK regulators' description of operational resilience, the management of disruption component requires firms to respond to disruptions, maintain trust among key stakeholders and communicate clearly during a crisis.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: In the UK regulators' description of operational resilience, the lessons learned component requires firms to learn from past events and to cover predictable shocks only.
cards.explanation: Lessons learned requires firms to learn from internal and external events and to improve resilience to unanticipated extreme shocks, not only predictable ones.
cards.originalText: Lessons learned: Firms should learn from past events and cover predictable shocks only
cards.correction: In the UK regulators' description of operational resilience, the lessons learned component requires firms to learn from past events and to improve resilience to unanticipated extreme shocks.

changes.to: improve resilience to unanticipated extreme shocks

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The Federal Reserve's 2020 sound practices for operational resilience require firms to reduce their reliance on third parties.
cards.explanation: The guidance asks firms to manage third-party risk to protect supply-chain resilience, not to cut their reliance on third parties.
cards.originalText: Firms are required to reduce their reliance on third parties.
cards.correction: The Federal Reserve's 2020 sound practices for operational resilience require firms to manage the risks of their reliance on third parties.

changes.from: reduce their reliance on third parties
changes.to: manage the risks of their reliance on third parties

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The Federal Reserve's 2020 sound practices expect firms to monitor and report on the coordination and maintenance of business continuity management and IT systems resilience.
cards.explanation: Business continuity management and IT systems resilience are pillars of operational resilience, and their coordination and maintenance must be monitored and reported.
cards.originalText: Firms should monitor and report on the coordination and maintenance of business continuity management (BCM) and IT systems resilience.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: A strong operational risk management framework is necessary in order to achieve operational resilience.
cards.explanation: Operational resilience is treated as a key outcome of an effective operational risk management framework, which is its central component.
cards.originalText: A strong ORM framework is necessary in order to achieve operational resilience.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The UK regulators' operational resilience approach is built around important business services, with impact tolerances tied to critical services rather than to individual processes.
cards.explanation: This is what distinguishes it from classic business continuity planning, which was process-based.
cards.originalText: Resilience is built around important business services, with impact tolerances tied to critical services rather than to processes per se.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational resilience concentrates solely on preventing disruptions, since severe disruptions are assumed to be avoidable with sufficient controls.
cards.explanation: Regulators and firms accept that severe disruptions will occur, so the approach moved from pure prevention to preventing, detecting and correcting incidents.
cards.originalText: Resilience concentrates solely on preventing disruptions, since severe disruptions are assumed to be avoidable with sufficient controls.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational resilience learns only from a firm's own internal incidents, since events at other organizations are not comparable.
cards.explanation: Lessons learned come from internal accidents and also from events made public at other organizations.
cards.originalText: Resilience learns only from the firm’s own internal incidents, since events at other organizations are not comparable.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: In the 2020 U.S. Federal Reserve guidance, third-party risk management and scenario analysis are among the building blocks of operational resilience.
cards.explanation: Third-party risk management supports supply-chain resilience and scenario analysis supports preparedness for tail events; both are supporting pillars of operational risk management.
cards.originalText: Among the necessary building blocks of operational resilience, the firm should include third‑party risk management and scenario analysis

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Incident management in an operational resilience framework involves establishing procedures for preventing all possible disruptions before they occur.
cards.explanation: Incident management is about response and recovery plans; firms accept that disruptions will occur and cannot all be prevented.
cards.originalText: Incident management involves establishing procedures for preventing all possible disruptions before they occur.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The best operational resilience framework is a significant one-time effort that requires no ongoing attention or maintenance once established.
cards.explanation: Coordination and maintenance of resilience activities must be monitored and reported, and firms must keep learning and improving.
cards.originalText: The best operational resilience framework is a significant one‑time effort that does not require ongoing attention or maintenance once it has been established

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The U.S. Federal Reserve issued its Sound Practices to Strengthen Operational Resilience in 2020.
cards.explanation: The Federal Reserve is one of the key regulators with official operational resilience guidance, alongside the UK authorities and the Basel Committee.
cards.originalText: U.S. Federal Reserve.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision issued its seven Principles for Operational Resilience in March 2021.
cards.explanation: The BCBS principles are one of the three main sets of official operational resilience guidance, alongside the UK and U.S. guidance.
cards.originalText: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: UK regulators expect firms to identify their important business services and develop an impact tolerance for each of them.
cards.explanation: An impact tolerance quantifies the amount of disruption that can be tolerated for each important business service.
cards.originalText: Develop an impact tolerance for each of the important business services provided by the firm.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Under UK operational resilience expectations, lines of communication should be established immediately after a breach incident has occurred.
cards.explanation: Communication must be planned in advance as part of management of disruption; setting it up only after an incident is too late.
cards.originalText: Immediately establish lines of communication after a breach incident has occurred.
cards.correction: Under UK operational resilience expectations, lines of communication should be established before a breach incident occurs.

changes.from: immediately after a breach incident has occurred

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: An operational resilience framework should consider the continuity of important business services in both extreme and nonextreme situations.
cards.explanation: Resilience is organised around important business services and must hold up in severe as well as ordinary disruptions.
cards.originalText: continuity of important business services in extreme and nonextreme situations.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: An operational resilience framework should consider the continuity of important business services in nonextreme situations only.
cards.explanation: Regulators expect extreme events to occur, infrequently, so the framework must cover extreme as well as nonextreme situations.
cards.originalText: continuity of important business services in nonextreme situations only.
cards.correction: An operational resilience framework should consider the continuity of important business services in both extreme and nonextreme situations.

changes.to: in both extreme and nonextreme situations

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: An operational resilience framework should be built on the continuity of each business process rather than on important business services.
cards.explanation: The old process-based view has been replaced by a service-based view centred on important business services.
cards.originalText: continuity of each business process and recovery on a timely basis in extreme and nonextreme situations.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: A bank should aim to prevent all severe operational disruptions through strong preventive controls, treating planning for response and recovery as secondary.
cards.explanation: Operational resilience assumes severe disruptions will occasionally occur, so frameworks balance preventing, detecting and correcting incidents rather than relying on prevention alone.
cards.originalText: The bank should aim to prevent all severe operational disruptions, because regulators expect that with strong enough preventive controls such disruptions will not occur, so planning for response and recovery is secondary.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Under operational resilience expectations, impact tolerance quantifies the amount of disruption that can be tolerated; it resembles a recovery time objective but is tied to critical services rather than individual processes.
cards.explanation: Impact tolerance is similar to a recovery time objective, but it applies to important business services rather than to processes.
cards.originalText: The bank should set impact tolerance levels by quantifying the amount of disruption that could be tolerated, which resembles a recovery time objective but is tied to critical services rather than individual processes.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Under operational resilience expectations, a bank should learn from its own incidents and from events made public at other firms and continuously improve its ability to withstand unanticipated extreme shocks.
cards.explanation: Lessons learned from internal and external events is what differentiates resilience from traditional business continuity.
cards.originalText: The bank should learn from its own incidents and from events made public at other firms and continuously improve its ability to withstand unanticipated extreme shocks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Validating the operational risk management framework and ensuring it is reviewed periodically is a responsibility of the board of directors rather than of senior management.
cards.explanation: The board approves the framework and ensures its periodic revision, and obtains assurance that senior management implements it effectively.
cards.originalText: Validating the ORMF and ensuring it is reviewed periodically, so that the bank’s operational risks are properly identified and managed.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Translating the operational risk management framework into specific policies and procedures that can be implemented and verified within each business unit is a responsibility of the board of directors rather than of senior management.
cards.explanation: This is implementation work that belongs to senior management; the board oversees it.
cards.originalText: Translating the ORMF into specific policies and procedures that can be implemented and verified within each business unit.
cards.correction: Translating the operational risk management framework into specific policies and procedures that can be implemented and verified within each business unit is a responsibility of senior management rather than of the board of directors.

changes.from: the board of directors rather than of senior management
changes.to: senior management rather than of the board of directors

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Recruiting experienced technical staff and ensuring sufficient operational risk training to implement the operational risk management framework is a responsibility of the board of directors rather than of senior management.
cards.explanation: Hiring and training staff to implement the framework is an executive task for senior management; the board only ensures adequate resources.
cards.originalText: Recruiting experienced technical staff and ensuring a sufficient level of operational risk training to implement the ORMF.
cards.correction: Recruiting experienced technical staff and ensuring sufficient operational risk training to implement the operational risk management framework is a responsibility of senior management rather than of the board of directors.

changes.from: the board of directors rather than of senior management
changes.to: senior management rather than of the board of directors

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The board of directors is ultimately responsible for operational risk management and resilience in a bank.
cards.explanation: Responsibility can be delegated but accountability cannot; the board owns operational risk and resilience and oversees management's execution.
cards.originalText: Board of directors.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The chief risk officer is ultimately responsible for operational risk management and resilience in a bank.
cards.explanation: The CRO is part of senior management and has delegated responsibility; ultimate responsibility rests with the board of directors.
cards.originalText: Chief risk officer.
cards.correction: The board of directors is ultimately responsible for operational risk management and resilience in a bank.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The board risk committee makes recommendations to the full board on risk exposures and risk-based decisions and reviews larger operational risk incidents escalated from lower committees.
cards.explanation: It sits at the top of the committee pyramid as a recommending and oversight body that advises the full board.
cards.originalText: Making recommendations to the full board on risk exposures and risk‑based decisions, and reviewing larger operational risk incidents escalated from lower committees.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The board risk committee sets the bank's risk appetite and approves the operational risk management framework without any reference to the full board.
cards.explanation: The full board sets risk appetite and validates the framework; the board risk committee only makes recommendations to it.
cards.originalText: Setting the bank’s risk appetite and approving the ORMF without any reference to the full board.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The senior management team, rather than the board of directors, is ultimately responsible for operational risk management and resilience.
cards.explanation: Senior management executes tasks delegated by the board and is accountable for them, but ultimate responsibility rests with the board of directors.
cards.originalText: The senior management team.
cards.correction: The board of directors, rather than the senior management team, is ultimately responsible for operational risk management and resilience.

changes.from: The senior management team, rather than the board of directors,
changes.to: The board of directors, rather than the senior management team,

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: A risk management unit that reports through a risk-generating business line, such as the head of credit, lacks independence and should instead have a reporting structure independent of the risk-generating units.
cards.explanation: The second line must be independent of the units that generate risk so that it can challenge them objectively.
cards.originalText: The RMU lacks independence because it reports through a risk‑generating business line; it should have a reporting structure independent of the risk‑generating units.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Placing a risk management unit inside a credit business unit improves its independence by bringing it closer to the risk it monitors.
cards.explanation: Embedding risk management in a business unit removes its independence and creates a self-review threat; the second line should be independent of risk-generating units.
cards.originalText: Independence would be improved by moving the RMU inside the credit unit so it sits closer to the risk it monitors.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Independent external auditors provide independent assurance to stakeholders such as regulators and investors from outside the bank's three internal lines of defense.
cards.explanation: External auditors sit outside the firm's internal lines, which is why they are sometimes informally called a fourth line.
cards.originalText: The independent external auditors

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: A bank's internal audit function is outside the three internal lines of defense.
cards.explanation: Internal audit is the third of the three internal lines of defense; the first line is the business and the second line is the risk oversight function.
cards.originalText: The bank’s internal audit function
cards.correction: A bank's internal audit function is the third of its three internal lines of defense.

changes.from: is outside the three internal lines of defense
changes.to: is the third of its three internal lines of defense

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Internal audit independently assesses the control system and compliance with policies across all departments, including the risk function, and reports to a non-executive director.
cards.explanation: As the third line, internal audit does not manage the risks it assesses and reports in solid line to a non-executive director such as the audit committee chair.
cards.originalText: Internal audit team.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Establishing risk management methods and measurement methods is a role of the second line of defense.
cards.explanation: The second line owns the methodology, while the first line owns the risks.
cards.originalText: Establishing risk management methods and measurement methods.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Making decisions for managing risks is a role of the second line of defense rather than of the first line.
cards.explanation: Risk-taking decisions belong to the first line; the second line challenges rather than decides.
cards.originalText: Making decisions for managing risks.
cards.correction: Making decisions for managing risks is a role of the first line of defense rather than of the second line.

changes.from: the second line of defense rather than of the first line
changes.to: the first line of defense rather than of the second line

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The second line of defense oversees the risk management activities of the third line of defense.
cards.explanation: The second line does not oversee internal audit; internal audit independently reviews the second line.
cards.originalText: Overseeing the risk management activities of the third line of defense.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: First-line risk owners monitor and report the operational risk profile of their business unit and escalate loss events and control deficiencies to the second line.
cards.explanation: Risk owners manage and report the risks they generate and escalate residual issues to the corporate operational risk function.
cards.originalText: Monitoring and reporting the operational risk profile of the business unit and escalating loss events and control deficiencies to the second line

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Developing and maintaining operational risk measurement policies, standards and guidelines is a role of the first line of defense.
cards.explanation: Policy and standard setting is a responsibility of the second line, the corporate operational risk function.
cards.originalText: Developing and maintaining operational risk measurement policies, standards and guidelines
cards.correction: Developing and maintaining operational risk measurement policies, standards and guidelines is a role of the second line of defense.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Challenging the consistency of business units' use of operational risk tools and providing evidence of that challenge is a role of the first line of defense.
cards.explanation: Effective challenge of business unit practice is the role of the second line.
cards.originalText: Challenging the consistency of the business units’ use of operational risk tools and providing evidence of that challenge
cards.correction: Challenging the consistency of business units' use of operational risk tools and providing evidence of that challenge is a role of the second line of defense.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: In the three lines of defense model, the first line defines the organization's risk appetite but should not attempt to directly influence its risk culture.
cards.explanation: Risk appetite is a board and senior management matter, and risk culture is shaped across the organization, including by the first line.
cards.originalText: The first line defines the organization’s risk appetite but should not attempt to directly influence its risk culture

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: In the three lines of defense model, the first line is responsible for implementing and maintaining effective controls to manage material operational risks.
cards.explanation: Risk owners in the first line identify risks and establish and assess the controls over them.
cards.originalText: The first line is responsible for implementing and maintaining effective controls to manage material operational risks

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: In the three lines of defense model, the second line is part of management and owns the operational risk methodology, while supporting the first line to help the firm create and protect value.
cards.explanation: The 2021 IIA model places the second line within management, providing expertise, support and challenge.
cards.originalText: The second line is part of management (and owns the ORM methodology) but provides support to the first line in order to help the firm create and protect value

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Internal audit cannot design or implement the operational risk management framework without compromising the independence of its assurance role.
cards.explanation: Internal audit's value is independent assurance over the first and second lines; designing the framework would mean reviewing its own work. Framework design belongs to the corporate operational risk function.
cards.originalText: Internal audit cannot design or implement the ORMF without compromising the independence of its assurance role.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Internal audit should report to the head of the corporate operational risk function in order to remain independent.
cards.explanation: Internal audit must be independent of risk management and report in solid line to a non-executive director, such as the audit committee chair.
cards.originalText: Internal audit should report to the head of the CORF in order to remain independent.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Business line management is not a line of defense.
cards.explanation: Business line management, as the risk owner, is the first line of defense.
cards.originalText: Business line management is not a line of defense.
cards.correction: Business line management is the first line of defense.

changes.from: is not a line of defense
changes.to: is the first line of defense

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The corporate operational risk function should not challenge the business lines' outputs because doing so creates a self-review threat.
cards.explanation: Challenging the first line's inputs and outputs is exactly the second line's job; a self-review threat arises only if the second line takes part in first-line activities or supplies the answers.
cards.originalText: The CORF should not challenge the business lines’ outputs because doing so creates a self‑review threat.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: To preserve its independence, the second line should give the first line the correct answers to its risk and control self-assessments before the first line completes them.
cards.explanation: The first line owns its assessments and the second line challenges them afterwards; supplying answers in advance creates a self-review threat and destroys independence.
cards.originalText: To preserve its independence, the second line should give the first line the correct answers to its risk and control self‑assessments before the first line completes them.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Internal audit should not rely exclusively on the work of risk management, compliance or finance, but should examine an appropriate sample of the activities itself.
cards.explanation: Internal audit may rely on others' work only after assessing its reliability, and must perform its own independent testing.
cards.originalText: Internal audit should not rely exclusively on the work of risk management, compliance, or finance, but should examine an appropriate sample of the activities itself.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: What defines a line of defense is the role and responsibility a function performs, not the name of its department.
cards.explanation: Because lines are defined by roles, hybrid functions arise, and their first-line and second-line duties should be documented and kept distinct.
cards.originalText: What defines a line of defense is the role and responsibility performed by a function, not the name of its department.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under the three lines of defense model, business line managers as the first line have the authority to take on risk exposures within the bank's risk appetite limits.
cards.explanation: Risk is owned by the business, but only within the limits set by the board's risk appetite.
cards.originalText: Business line managers, as the first line of defense, should have the authority to take on risk exposures within the bank’s risk appetite limits.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under the three lines of defense model, the risk management function should approve every transaction that creates a new risk exposure for the bank.
cards.explanation: That would pull the second line into first-line decision making; the second line challenges and may veto breaches of limits, it does not approve every transaction.
cards.originalText: The risk management function should approve every transaction that creates a new risk exposure for the bank.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under the three lines of defense model, the third line should continuously monitor the implementation of the risk management framework.
cards.explanation: Continuous monitoring is a second-line activity; internal audit remains independent and provides periodic assurance.
cards.originalText: The third line of defense should continuously monitor the implementation of the ERM framework to ensure its effectiveness.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Reviewing and taking part in the monitoring and reporting of the operational risk profile is a task of the second line of defense.
cards.explanation: The corporate operational risk function reviews and contributes to monitoring and reporting of the operational risk profile as part of its oversight role.
cards.originalText: Reviewing and taking part in the monitoring and reporting of the operational risk profile.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Identifying risks and controls in accordance with the group definitions is a task of the second line of defense rather than of the first line.
cards.explanation: Mapping risks and controls is carried out in the first line; the second line only challenges it.
cards.originalText: Identifying risks and controls in accordance with the group definitions.
cards.correction: Identifying risks and controls in accordance with the group definitions is a task of the first line of defense rather than of the second line.

changes.from: the second line of defense rather than of the first line
changes.to: the first line of defense rather than of the second line

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: When the three lines of defense model is applied to model risk management, model developers and model owners, as risk owners, form the first line of defense.
cards.explanation: The first line owns and manages the risk it generates; the second line independently challenges it.
cards.originalText: Model developers and model owners, as risk owners, form the first line of defense

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: When the three lines of defense model is applied to model risk management, the second line of defense owns the model risk it oversees.
cards.explanation: The first line, not the second, owns the risk; the second line oversees and challenges it independently.
cards.originalText: The second line of defense owns the model risk it oversees

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe the “three lines of defense” model for operational risk governance and compare roles and responsibilities for each line of defense.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: In model risk management, the second line of defense should help the first line build the models and co-sign their validation so as to ensure consistency.
