cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel Committee enhanced the CVA framework in order to improve its risk sensitivity by recognizing more risk drivers, such as the exposure component and eligible hedges.
cards.explanation: The enhanced framework pursues risk sensitivity (more risk drivers), robustness (internal models removed) and consistency with the revised market risk framework.
cards.originalText: Enhance the risk sensitivity of the framework by recognizing more risk drivers.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: In the revised standardized approach for credit risk, risk weights on residential real estate exposures are lower when the loan-to-value ratio falls into a lower band.
cards.explanation: Residential mortgage risk weights now depend on the LTV band, for example rising from 20% below 50% LTV to 70% above 100% LTV for whole loans, so a lower LTV means a lower risk weight.
cards.originalText: In the SA for residential real estate exposures, risk weights are lower when the loan‑to‑value (LTV) ratio falls into a lower band.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The revised standardized approach for credit risk eliminated the treatment of unrated exposures, because all exposures are now required to have an external credit rating.
cards.explanation: The revisions reduced reliance on external ratings but kept a more granular treatment of unrated exposures. They did not require every exposure to be rated.
cards.originalText: The SA eliminated the treatment of unrated exposures because all exposures are now required to have an external credit rating.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The December 2017 revisions removed the foundation IRB (F-IRB) option, because the advanced IRB (A-IRB) approach must be used for all asset classes.
cards.explanation: This reverses the reform. A-IRB was removed for large corporates, banks and other financial institutions, for which F-IRB or the standardized approach must be used.
cards.originalText: The IRB framework removed the foundation IRB (F‑IRB) option because the advanced IRB (A‑IRB) must be used for all asset classes.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The December 2017 revisions removed the IRB parameter input floors (PD, LGD, EAD) in order to increase RWA variability across banks.
cards.explanation: Input floors were introduced, and their purpose is to reduce unwarranted variability in risk-weighted assets across banks.
cards.originalText: The IRB framework removed the parameter input floors (PD, LGD, EAD) to increase RWA variability across banks.
cards.correction: The December 2017 revisions introduced IRB parameter input floors (PD, LGD, EAD) in order to reduce RWA variability across banks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the December 2017 revisions, the new standardized approach for operational risk eliminated a bank's historical internal loss experience as an input, because it was uncorrelated with actual operational losses.
cards.explanation: The new standardized approach uses a measure of income and a measure of historical losses, and past losses are assumed to be positively related to future losses.
cards.originalText: For operational risk, the new standardized approach eliminated the bank’s historical internal loss experience as an input because it was uncorrelated with actual operational losses.
cards.correction: Under the December 2017 revisions, the new standardized approach for operational risk retained a bank's historical internal loss experience as an input, because it is positively related to future operational losses.

changes.from: because it was uncorrelated with actual operational losses
changes.to: because it is positively related to future operational losses

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The December 2017 revisions to the CVA framework were designed to enhance its risk sensitivity, strengthen its robustness and improve its consistency with the market risk framework.
cards.explanation: These three goals drove the CVA reform: more risk drivers, removal of internal models, and alignment with the revised market risk framework.
cards.originalText: The CVA framework was revised to enhance its risk sensitivity, strengthen its robustness, and improve its consistency with the market risk framework.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: For operational risk, the Basel III revisions replaced the previous standardized approaches and the advanced measurement approach with a single risk-sensitive standardized approach for all banks.
cards.explanation: The AMA and the three older standardized approaches were replaced by one new standardized approach.
cards.originalText: For operational risk, the previous standardized approaches and the advanced measurement approach were replaced by a single risk‑sensitive standardized approach for all banks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the revised output floor, a bank's RWA calculated with internal models cannot be lower than 72.5% of the RWA calculated using only standardized approaches.
cards.explanation: The output floor is a backstop calibrated at 72.5% of standardized-approach RWA, limiting the capital benefit of internal models.
cards.originalText: Under the revised output floor, a bank’s RWA under internal models cannot be lower than 72.5% of the RWA calculated using only standardized approaches.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the revised Basel III standardized approach for credit risk, banks assign residential mortgages different risk weights based on each mortgage's loan-to-value ratio.
cards.explanation: Under Basel II one risk weight applied to all residential mortgages. The revised standardized approach makes the weight depend on the LTV ratio.
cards.originalText: Assign different credit risk weights for residential mortgages based on each mortgage’s loan‑to‑value ratio.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the revised Basel III framework, a bank may introduce an internally created model to determine its operational risk capital.
cards.explanation: Internal models (the AMA) for operational risk were eliminated. A single standardized approach based on income and historical losses is the only approach allowed.
cards.originalText: Introduce an internally created model to determine the bank’s operational risk capital.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the revised Basel III framework, banks may apply the advanced internal ratings-based approach to exposures to banks and large corporations.
cards.explanation: A-IRB is no longer permitted for exposures to banks, financial institutions and large and mid-size corporates. The foundation IRB or the standardized approach must be used instead.
cards.originalText: Apply the advanced internal rating‑based approach for certain types of credit exposures, such as exposures to banks and large corporations.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel III reforms restricted the use of internal model approaches for systemic risk.
cards.explanation: Internal model approaches were restricted for credit risk, CVA risk and operational risk. Systemic risk has no internal model approach and is addressed through the G-SIB leverage ratio buffer.
cards.originalText: systemic risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel III reforms restricted the use of internal model approaches for credit risk.
cards.explanation: The advanced IRB approach was removed for large and mid-size corporates, banks and other financial institutions.
cards.originalText: credit risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel III reforms restricted the use of internal model approaches for operational risk.
cards.explanation: The advanced measurement approach was eliminated in favor of a single standardized approach.
cards.originalText: operational risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel III reforms restricted the use of internal model approaches for credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk.
cards.explanation: The internal model approach to CVA risk was removed, leaving SA-CVA or the basic approach.
cards.originalText: credit valuation risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel III reforms introduced a leverage ratio buffer for global systemically important banks.
cards.explanation: The revised leverage ratio framework adds a buffer that applies to G-SIBs and must be met with Tier 1 capital.
cards.originalText: global systemically important banks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel III reforms introduced a leverage ratio buffer for all global banks.
cards.explanation: The leverage ratio buffer applies only to global systemically important banks, not to all global banks.
cards.originalText: global banks.
cards.correction: The Basel III reforms introduced a leverage ratio buffer for global systemically important banks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III reforms, the advanced IRB approach is no longer permitted for residential and commercial real estate exposures.
cards.explanation: A-IRB was removed only for large and mid-size corporate exposures and for banks and other financial institutions. It remains available for real estate exposures.
cards.originalText: residential and commercial real estate.
cards.correction: Under the Basel III reforms, the advanced IRB approach remains permitted for residential and commercial real estate exposures.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III reforms, the advanced IRB approach is no longer permitted for large corporate exposures.
cards.explanation: A-IRB was removed for large corporates, which must use the foundation IRB or the standardized approach.
cards.originalText: large corporate exposures.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III reforms, the advanced IRB approach is no longer permitted for mid-size corporate exposures.
cards.explanation: A-IRB was removed for large and mid-size corporates alike.
cards.originalText: mid‑size corporate exposures.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III reforms, the advanced IRB approach is no longer permitted for exposures to banks and other financial institutions.
cards.explanation: A-IRB was removed for banks and other financial institutions, which must use the foundation IRB or the standardized approach.
cards.originalText: banks and other financial institutions.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III reforms, a bank's operational risk capital requirement is determined by measures of its income and its historical operational risk losses.
cards.explanation: The single standardized approach uses income and historical losses, both assumed to be positively related to future operational risk.
cards.originalText: income and historical operational risk losses.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III reforms, a bank's operational risk capital requirement is determined by measures of its income and its expected operational risk losses.
cards.explanation: The framework uses actual historical operational risk losses, not modelled expected losses.
cards.originalText: income and expected operational risk losses.
cards.correction: Under the Basel III reforms, a bank's operational risk capital requirement is determined by measures of its income and its historical operational risk losses.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III reforms, a bank's operational risk capital requirement is determined by measures of its leverage and income.
cards.explanation: Leverage is not an input to operational risk capital. The inputs are income and historical operational risk losses.
cards.originalText: leverage and income.
cards.correction: Under the Basel III reforms, a bank's operational risk capital requirement is determined by measures of its historical operational risk losses and income.

changes.to: historical operational risk losses and income

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel Committee's IRB enhancements increase the haircuts applied to collateral for secured exposures and reduce the supervisory LGD for unsecured exposures to non-financial corporates from 45% to 40%.
cards.explanation: Under the foundation IRB approach, haircuts on collateral rise and the unsecured LGD for non-financial corporates falls from 45% to 40%.
cards.originalText: Secured exposures: increasing the haircuts that apply to the collateral; Unsecured exposures: reducing the LGD parameter from 45% to 40% for exposures to non‑financial corporates.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Summarize the December 2017 revisions to the Basel III framework in the following areas: - The standardized approach to credit risk - The internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk - The CVA risk framework - The operational risk framework - The leverage ratio framework
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel Committee's IRB enhancements decrease the haircuts applied to collateral for secured exposures.
cards.explanation: The enhancements increase, not decrease, the haircuts that apply to collateral under the foundation IRB approach.
cards.originalText: Secured exposures: decreasing the haircuts that apply to the collateral; Unsecured exposures: reducing the LGD parameter from 45% to 40% for exposures to non‑financial corporates.
cards.correction: The Basel Committee's IRB enhancements increase the haircuts applied to collateral for secured exposures.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Describe the revised output floor introduced as part of the Basel III reforms and approaches to be used when calculating the output floor.
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel III output floor sets a minimum level of risk-weighted assets.
cards.explanation: The floor puts a lower bound, 72.5% of the RWA calculated with standardized approaches, on total RWA, limiting the capital benefit of internal models.
cards.originalText: risk‑weighted assets.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Describe the revised output floor introduced as part of the Basel III reforms and approaches to be used when calculating the output floor.
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The Basel III output floor sets a minimum level of leverage.
cards.explanation: Leverage is governed by the separate leverage ratio framework, with a G-SIB buffer. The output floor applies to risk-weighted assets.
cards.originalText: leverage.
cards.correction: The Basel III output floor sets a minimum level of risk-weighted assets.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Describe the revised output floor introduced as part of the Basel III reforms and approaches to be used when calculating the output floor.
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The internal ratings-based (IRB-CVA) approach can be used when calculating the output floor for CVA risk under the Basel III reforms.
cards.explanation: The output floor relies on standardized approaches only. For CVA risk the permitted choices are SA-CVA, BA-CVA or 100% of the counterparty credit risk capital requirement.
cards.originalText: the internal ratings‑based (IRB‑CVA) approach.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Describe the revised output floor introduced as part of the Basel III reforms and approaches to be used when calculating the output floor.
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The basic approach (BA-CVA) can be used when calculating the output floor for CVA risk under the Basel III reforms.
cards.explanation: BA-CVA is a standardized approach and is permitted in the floor calculation.
cards.originalText: the basic (BA‑CVA) approach.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Describe the revised output floor introduced as part of the Basel III reforms and approaches to be used when calculating the output floor.
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: The standardized approach (SA-CVA) can be used when calculating the output floor for CVA risk under the Basel III reforms.
cards.explanation: SA-CVA is a standardized approach and is permitted in the floor calculation.
cards.originalText: the standardized (SA‑CVA) approach.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.loText: Describe the revised output floor introduced as part of the Basel III reforms and approaches to be used when calculating the output floor.
cards.reading: ORR-23: High-level Summary of Basel III Reforms
cards.statement: When calculating the output floor for CVA risk, a bank may use 100% of its counterparty credit risk capital requirement.
cards.explanation: Using 100% of the counterparty credit risk capital requirement is an explicitly permitted alternative to SA-CVA and BA-CVA for the floor.
cards.originalText: 100% of the bank’s counterparty credit risk capital requirement.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Outsourcing a function to a third-party provider transfers responsibility for its disruption to the provider, so the bank need not set its own impact tolerance for the service.
cards.explanation: Outsourcing does not transfer responsibility. The institution remains ultimately responsible and must manage the third-party dependency, including setting an impact tolerance for the important business service.
cards.originalText: The payment bank was more vulnerable, but outsourcing payment processing to the cloud provider transfers responsibility for the disruption, so the bank need not set its own impact tolerance.
cards.correction: Outsourcing a function to a third-party provider does not transfer responsibility for its disruption to the provider, so the bank must still set its own impact tolerance for the service.

changes.from: to the provider, so the bank need not set
changes.to: to the provider, so the bank must still set

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Sufficiently strong preventive IT controls can stop severe operational disruptions to a digital service from ever occurring.
cards.explanation: Severe disruptions are accepted as occasionally inevitable. Operational resilience requires detection, response and recovery, not prevention alone.
cards.originalText: The payment bank was less vulnerable, because suﬀiciently strong preventive IT controls can stop severe operational disruptions to a digital service from ever occurring.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe operational resilience, identify the elements of an operational resilience framework, and summarize regulatory expectations for operational resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational resilience is assessed process by process, so each bank should set recovery time objectives for its internal processes rather than for its services.
cards.explanation: UK regulators moved from a process-based view of continuity to a service-based view, in which firms identify important business services and set impact tolerances for them.
cards.originalText: Neither can be ranked, because resilience is assessed process by process, so each bank should set recovery time objectives for its internal processes rather than for its services.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under regulatory expectations modelled on the BCBS Principles for Operational Resilience, the board oversees senior management's implementation of the resilience approach, ensures sufficient financial and technical resources, and receives timely reporting on deficiencies.
cards.explanation: BCBS Principle 1 asks directors to oversee implementation, ensure adequate financial and technical resources are allocated, and receive timely reporting, particularly on deficiencies that could affect critical operations.
cards.originalText: The board should oversee senior management’s implementation of the resilience approach, ensure suﬀicient financial and technical resources, and receive timely reporting on deficiencies.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under the BCBS Principles for Operational Resilience, the board should create a governance structure for resilience separate from its existing risk committees.
cards.explanation: The principle is for directors to use their existing governance structure to establish, oversee and implement the resilience approach, not to build a parallel one.
cards.originalText: The board should create a governance structure for resilience separate from its existing risk committees, so that resilience is not diluted by routine operational risk business.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under the BCBS Principles for Operational Resilience, the board should hear about resilience only after a severe disruption, and its members need no specific training in resilience.
cards.explanation: The board should receive ongoing, timely reporting from senior management, and the firm must be able to show that board members have been trained.
cards.originalText: The board should hear about resilience only after a severe disruption, and its members need no specific training in resilience as long as senior management is trained.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under the BCBS Principles for Operational Resilience, a bank should calibrate its resilience approach only to disruptions it has already experienced and leave out any scenario more severe than its own history.
cards.explanation: The resilience approach must consider a broad range of severe but plausible scenarios, including ones the bank has never experienced.
cards.originalText: The board should calibrate the resilience approach to disruptions the bank has already experienced, leaving out any scenario more severe than its own history.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The board ultimately owns the operational risk limits and validates them periodically, often delegating this to the board risk committee, which relies on the risk function to implement and report on them.
cards.explanation: In practice the board delegates ownership of limits to the board risk committee, which in turn requests the support of the risk function.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The group operational risk committee sits at the top of the committee structure and makes recommendations directly to the full board on risk-based decisions, risk exposure and risk management.
cards.explanation: The board risk committee, not the group operational risk committee, sits at the top and makes recommendations to the full board. The group committee reports upward to the executive and board risk committees.
cards.originalText: The group operational risk committee sits at the top of the structure and makes recommendations directly to the full board on risk-based decisions, risk exposure and risk management.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: A risk appetite statement is credible on its own, without being tied to specific key controls or to monitoring metrics.
cards.explanation: A statement such as minimal tolerance for data breaches must be corroborated by strong key controls and monitored through indicators on exposure, controls and losses.
cards.originalText: A statement of minimal tolerance for data breaches is credible on its own, since an appetite statement need not be tied to specific key controls or to monitoring metrics.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Describe and compare the roles of different committees and the board of directors in operational risk governance.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Senior management approves and periodically reviews the operational risk appetite and tolerance statement, and the board receives the approved statement for information.
cards.explanation: The board approves and periodically reviews the risk appetite and tolerance statement, while senior management develops and implements the policies and systems.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain best practices and regulatory expectations for the development of a risk appetite for operational risk and for a strong risk culture.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Business managers discussing internal incidents openly in team meetings, without undue blame, so that the whole unit learns from them, is a strong sign of a healthy risk culture.
cards.explanation: The most telling sign of risk culture is arguably the capacity to talk about internal incidents without undue blame or embarrassment, for collective learning and improvement.
cards.originalText: Business managers discuss internal incidents openly in team meetings, without undue blame, so that the whole unit learns from them.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain best practices and regulatory expectations for the development of a risk appetite for operational risk and for a strong risk culture.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: A year with no operational incidents reported by relationship managers, during a period of record growth in client assets, is a sign of a healthy risk culture.
cards.explanation: Zero reported incidents amid record growth is a warning sign of under-reporting, resistance to bad news and target pressure, not a strength.
cards.originalText: No operational incidents have been reported by the relationship managers over the past year, a year of record growth in client assets.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain best practices and regulatory expectations for the development of a risk appetite for operational risk and for a strong risk culture.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Senior managers can be exempt from annual risk training because they already set the tone at the top through their own conduct.
cards.explanation: A healthy risk culture applies the same rules to everyone, and regulators expect formal, regular training for senior managers too.
cards.originalText: Senior managers are exempt from the annual risk training, since they already set the tone at the top through their own conduct.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A customer's slip and fall on a wet floor in a bank branch, with the bank paying the personal injury claim, is classified under Employment Practices and Workplace Safety, Safe Environment.
cards.explanation: General liability events such as slip and fall, including the payment of personal injury claims, fall under EPWS / Safe Environment.
cards.originalText: A customer slipped on a wet floor in one of the bank’s branches, and the bank paid the personal injury claim: EPWS, Safe Environment.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A relationship manager who takes on a corporate client without the required investigation and lets its exposure exceed the approved limit is classified under Execution, Delivery and Process Management, Customer Intake and Documentation.
cards.explanation: Failure to investigate a client per guidelines and exceeding client exposure limits belong to Clients, Products and Business Practices, Selection, Sponsorship and Exposure. Customer Intake and Documentation covers missing client permissions and legal documents.
cards.originalText: A relationship manager took on a corporate client without the investigation the guidelines require and let its exposure exceed the approved limit: EDPM, Customer Intake and Documentation.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A fine imposed because a bank failed to submit a mandatory regulatory report on time is classified under Clients, Products and Business Practices, Improper Business or Market Practices.
cards.explanation: A failed mandatory reporting obligation is Execution, Delivery and Process Management, Monitoring and Reporting. The fine is an impact, not the event type.
cards.originalText: The bank was fined after it failed to submit a mandatory regulatory report by the deadline: CPBP, Improper Business or Market Practices.
cards.correction: A fine imposed because a bank failed to submit a mandatory regulatory report on time is classified under Execution, Delivery and Process Management, Monitoring and Reporting.

changes.from: Clients, Products and Business Practices, Improper Business or Market Practices
changes.to: Execution, Delivery and Process Management, Monitoring and Reporting

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A settlement paid by a bank after a contractual dispute with its outsourced IT provider over service levels is classified under Business Disruption and System Failures, Systems.
cards.explanation: No system failed. Outsourcing and vendor disputes belong to Execution, Delivery and Process Management, Vendors and Suppliers, while BDSF / Systems covers hardware, software, telecommunications and utility outages.
cards.originalText: A contractual dispute with the bank’s outsourced IT provider over service levels ended in a settlement paid by the bank: BDSF, Systems.
cards.correction: A settlement paid by a bank after a contractual dispute with its outsourced IT provider over service levels is classified under Execution, Delivery and Process Management, Vendors and Suppliers.

changes.from: Business Disruption and System Failures, Systems
changes.to: Execution, Delivery and Process Management, Vendors and Suppliers

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A trader deliberately executing a transaction type outside his mandate, not reporting it, and causing a monetary loss is classified under Internal Fraud, Unauthorised Activity.
cards.explanation: Unauthorised Activity covers an insider deliberately acting beyond his authority, such as unreported or unauthorised transactions with monetary loss and intentional mismarking of positions.
cards.originalText: A trader deliberately executed a transaction type outside his mandate, did not report it, and the bank lost money unwinding it.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A branch teller embezzling cash from customers' dormant accounts over several years is classified under Internal Fraud, Unauthorised Activity.
cards.explanation: Embezzlement is a deliberate taking of value by an insider and falls under Internal Fraud, Theft and Fraud. Unauthorised Activity covers acting beyond authority in the firm's business.
cards.originalText: A branch teller embezzled cash from customers’ dormant accounts over several years.
cards.correction: A branch teller embezzling cash from customers' dormant accounts over several years is classified under Internal Fraud, Theft and Fraud.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A pricing model error embedded in a structured deposit product that leads to client compensation is classified under Clients, Products and Business Practices, Product Flaws.
cards.explanation: Model errors in a product's design are a Level 3 example under CPBP / Product Flaws, whereas a mistake in operating a model during processing would be Execution, Delivery and Process Management.
cards.originalText: The pricing model error: Level 1 Clients, Products and Business Practices; Level 2 Product Flaws.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: An employee trading on inside information for his personal account is classified under Clients, Products and Business Practices, Improper Business or Market Practices.
cards.explanation: Insider trading not on the firm's account is Internal Fraud, Theft and Fraud. Only insider trading on the firm's account is CPBP / Improper Business or Market Practices.
cards.originalText: The insider trading event: Level 1 Clients, Products and Business Practices; Level 2 Improper Business or Market Practices.
cards.correction: An employee trading on inside information for his personal account is classified under Internal Fraud, Theft and Fraud.

changes.from: Clients, Products and Business Practices, Improper Business or Market Practices

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A customer acting alone who kites cheques between accounts at the bank and at another bank is classified under Internal Fraud, Theft and Fraud.
cards.explanation: Internal fraud requires at least one internal party. A customer acting alone is a third party, so check kiting is External Fraud, Theft and Fraud.
cards.originalText: The cheque kiting event: Level 1 Internal Fraud; Level 2 Theft and Fraud.
cards.correction: A customer acting alone who kites cheques between accounts at the bank and at another bank is classified under External Fraud, Theft and Fraud.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply the Level 1, 2, and 3 categories in the Basel operational risk taxonomy.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A utility power outage that halts a bank's main data centre without damaging equipment is classified under Damage to Physical Assets, Disasters and Other Events.
cards.explanation: Damage to Physical Assets requires loss or damage to physical assets. A utility outage with no damage is Business Disruption and System Failures, Systems.
cards.originalText: The utility outage: Level 1 Damage to Physical Assets; Level 2 Disasters and Other Events.
cards.correction: A utility power outage that halts a bank's main data centre without damaging equipment is classified under Business Disruption and System Failures, Systems.

changes.from: Damage to Physical Assets, Disasters and Other Events
changes.to: Business Disruption and System Failures, Systems

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe approaches used to determine the level of operational risk capital for economic capital purposes, including their application and limitations.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: Linear discriminant analysis is a scoring tool that classifies borrowers into credit-quality groups, whereas the loss distribution approach combines frequency and severity distributions into an annual loss distribution whose 99.9th percentile sets stand-alone operational risk capital.
cards.explanation: The two share the acronym LDA but belong to different fields: Altman-style discriminant scoring classifies borrowers, while the loss distribution approach sizes operational risk capital.
cards.originalText: Document 1 applies linear discriminant analysis, a scoring tool; document 2 applies the loss distribution approach, whose 99.9th percentile sets stand-alone capital.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe approaches used to determine the level of operational risk capital for economic capital purposes, including their application and limitations.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: Under the loss distribution approach, no external data or scenarios are needed, because splitting each loss into frequency and severity doubles the observations available for the tail.
cards.explanation: The split does give more data points, but it is not sufficient to account for the extreme skewness of operational losses, so the tail still needs external data and scenario analysis.
cards.originalText: Document 2 needs no external data or scenarios, because splitting each loss into frequency and severity doubles the observations available for the tail.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: UK regulators were first to publish on operational resilience, with a 2018 paper that moved from a process-based to a service-based view, and the 2021 BCBS principles treat resilience as an outcome of effective operational risk management.
cards.explanation: The Bank of England, PRA and FCA discussion paper of July 2018 introduced important business services. The BCBS Principles for Operational Resilience followed in March 2021.
cards.originalText: UK regulators were first, with a 2018 paper that moved from a process-based to a service-based view; the 2021 BCBS principles treat resilience as an outcome of effective operational risk management.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: The BCBS issued the first operational resilience guidance in 2018, and UK regulators then turned its seven principles into the concepts of important business services and impact tolerances.
cards.explanation: The order is reversed. UK regulators published first, in 2018, and the BCBS principles followed in 2021.
cards.originalText: The BCBS issued the first resilience guidance in 2018; UK regulators then turned its seven principles into the concepts of important business services and impact tolerances.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: Operational resilience requirements replace the existing operational risk management requirements, because they assume that strong preventive controls can stop severe disruptions from occurring.
cards.explanation: Resilience requirements supplement rather than replace the existing framework, and the industry mindset moved away from pure prevention after accepting that severe disruptions will sometimes occur.
cards.originalText: The resilience requirements replace the existing operational risk management requirements, because they assume that strong preventive controls can stop severe disruptions from occurring.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: A bank that relies on a single third-party provider in one region for several important business services should treat the provider as a single point of failure, map each service end to end, track key-supplier dependency as a key risk indicator and keep an exit strategy with comparable providers.
cards.explanation: Concentration risk arises when outsourced services rely on few providers or few locations, so the bank must map dependencies, monitor them and plan an exit.
cards.originalText: The bank should treat the provider as a single point of failure: map each important business service end to end, track key-supplier dependency as a KRI, and keep an exit strategy with comparable providers.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: Concentration risk in outsourcing refers only to systemic risk for the banking industry from many banks using the same provider, so it is a matter for supervisors rather than for the individual bank to manage.
cards.explanation: Concentration risk also arises at firm level when a bank's own services depend on few providers or few locations, and the bank must manage it.
cards.originalText: Concentration risk here refers only to systemic risk for the banking industry from many banks using the same provider, so it is a matter for supervisors rather than for the bank to manage.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: A bank can reduce the frequency of its monitoring of a critical third-party provider and rely on the provider's own controls, because the provider is a large, reputable firm with strong built-in security.
cards.explanation: A risk-based rating makes a critical, hard-to-substitute provider higher risk, which requires more frequent and stringent monitoring. Built-in cloud controls do not remove the need for the bank's own oversight.
cards.originalText: Because the provider is a large, reputable firm with strong built-in security, the bank can reduce the frequency of its monitoring and place reliance on the provider’s own controls.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: Under operational resilience rules, the unit of tolerance to be tested is the recovery time objective of each internal process.
cards.explanation: Process-level recovery time objectives belong to business continuity management. Operational resilience is articulated around important business services and their impact tolerances.
cards.originalText: The bank should set a recovery time objective for each internal process the provider supports, since under resilience rules the process-level RTO is the unit of tolerance to be tested.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: When a severe but plausible scenario test shows that an important business service would be restored beyond its impact tolerance, the bank should examine the lessons learned, act on the weakness found, such as a key-person dependency, and retest.
cards.explanation: Where an impact tolerance is exceeded, firms examine lessons from stress tests and take action, for example by documenting procedures and training a back-up, then test again.
cards.originalText: Examine the lessons learned, act on the key-person dependency, for example by documenting procedures and training a back-up, then retest.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: When testing shows that an important business service is restored later than its impact tolerance, the bank should raise the impact tolerance to match the recovery time it has shown it can achieve.
cards.explanation: Resetting the tolerance to tested capability would accept the very harm the tolerance is meant to prevent. The bank should improve its recovery capability instead.
cards.originalText: Raise the impact tolerance to 30 hours, so that the tolerance matches the recovery time the bank has shown it can achieve.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: Operational resilience testing should cover only non-extreme situations.
cards.explanation: Scenarios should be severe but plausible. Only the most extreme conditions fall outside the scope of resilience testing.
cards.originalText: Replace the scenario with a milder one, because resilience testing should cover only nonextreme situations.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.loText: Describe and explain the steps to ensure a strong level of operational resilience, and to test the operational resilience of important business services.
cards.reading: ORR-4: Risk Measurement and Assessment
cards.statement: Holding additional operational risk capital brings an important business service back within its impact tolerance.
cards.explanation: Capital absorbs losses but does not restore a service faster, so the shortfall against the impact tolerance remains.
cards.originalText: Hold additional operational risk capital against the six-hour shortfall, which brings the service back within its tolerance.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Describe current practices by banks and supervisors in the governance of a cyber-risk management framework, including roles and responsibilities.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Having the chief information security officer report to the chief risk officer is common but not ideal, because the CRO may favour compliance over innovation; some global banks now have the CISO report to the CEO or the board.
cards.explanation: In most cases the CISO reports to the CRO or CIO with no independent line to the CEO or board. The Basel Committee case study calls the CRO placement not ideal because of the CRO's compliance emphasis.
cards.originalText: The arrangement is common but not ideal, since the CRO may favour compliance over innovation; some global banks now have the CISO report to the CEO or board.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Describe current practices by banks and supervisors in the governance of a cyber-risk management framework, including roles and responsibilities.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: At most large banks, the chief information security officer already has an independent reporting line to the board.
cards.explanation: In most cases the CISO reports to the CRO or the CIO, with no independent reporting line to the CEO or the board.
cards.originalText: The bank is an outlier, since at most large banks the CISO already has an independent reporting line to the board.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Describe current practices by banks and supervisors in the governance of a cyber-risk management framework, including roles and responsibilities.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Having the chief information security officer report to the chief risk officer is the preferred arrangement, because the CRO's emphasis on compliance gives risk-based cyber controls the strongest support.
cards.explanation: The Basel Committee case study calls this placement not ideal precisely because the CRO's emphasis on compliance may come at the expense of innovation.
cards.originalText: The arrangement is the preferred one, since the CRO’s emphasis on compliance gives risk-based cyber controls the strongest support.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Describe current practices by banks and supervisors in the governance of a cyber-risk management framework, including roles and responsibilities.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Regulators such as SAMA require the cybersecurity function to sit within the IT function, so the chief information security officer should report to the CIO.
cards.explanation: SAMA requires a cyber-security function that is independent from the IT function, with its own budget and staff evaluations, reporting to the CEO or managing director or to a senior level.
cards.originalText: The arrangement should move to the CIO, since regulators such as SAMA require the cybersecurity function to sit within the IT function.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Describe current practices by banks and supervisors in the governance of a cyber-risk management framework, including roles and responsibilities.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Most regulators do not require a standalone cyber-security strategy, but all of them expect a board-approved information security strategy, policy and procedures.
cards.explanation: According to the Basel Committee range-of-practices report, all regulators expect a board-approved information security strategy, policy and procedures under the broad remit of effective oversight.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Describe current practices by banks and supervisors in the governance of a cyber-risk management framework, including roles and responsibilities.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Most regulators require banks to implement the three lines of defence model for cyber risk and prescribe how cyber responsibilities are distributed across the three lines.
cards.explanation: Regulators use the three lines of defence model to assess cyber risk, but most neither require it nor prescribe how responsibilities are split.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Describe current practices by banks and supervisors in the governance of a cyber-risk management framework, including roles and responsibilities.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Of the five types of cyber-security information sharing, sharing among regulators is the most widely observed.
cards.explanation: Sharing among regulators is the least observed type, with ad hoc channels such as supervisory colleges and memoranda of understanding.
cards.originalText: Of the five types of cyber-security information sharing, sharing among regulators is the most widely observed, mainly through supervisory colleges and memoranda of understanding.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Describe current practices by banks and supervisors in the governance of a cyber-risk management framework, including roles and responsibilities.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: The Equifax breach exploited a vulnerability for which no patch had yet been released, so the main lesson is to invest in threat intelligence rather than in patch management.
cards.explanation: At Equifax the patch had been released days earlier. The failures were patch enforcement and asset inventory, not a zero-day attack.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain methods for supervising cyber-resilience, testing and incident response approaches, and cybersecurity and resilience metrics.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Supervisors scope cyber-resilience reviews by each bank's scale, complexity, business model and past findings, and trigger them from the bank's own risk assessments, inspection findings and incidents.
cards.explanation: Most supervisors focus on key risks such as cyber in the context of scale, complexity, business model and previous findings, and reviews are often triggered by risk assessments, inspections and incidents.
cards.originalText: Scope reviews by each bank’s scale, complexity, business model and past findings, and trigger them from its own risk assessments, inspection findings and incidents.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain methods for supervising cyber-resilience, testing and incident response approaches, and cybersecurity and resilience metrics.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Supervisors rely on one harmonised international taxonomy of cyber-risk controls to find gaps in supervisory coverage, as jurisdiction-specific taxonomies have been phased out.
cards.explanation: Taxonomies are currently jurisdiction-specific and do not rely on harmonised concepts and definitions.
cards.originalText: Rely on one harmonised international taxonomy of cyber-risk controls to find gaps in supervisory coverage, as jurisdiction-specific taxonomies have been phased out.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain methods for supervising cyber-resilience, testing and incident response approaches, and cybersecurity and resilience metrics.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Supervisors limit assessments of information security controls to off-site desk reviews, since most jurisdictions no longer inspect these controls on site.
cards.explanation: Most jurisdictions undertake both off-site and on-site reviews and inspections of regulated institutions' information security controls.
cards.originalText: Limit assessments of information security controls to off-site desk reviews, since most jurisdictions no longer inspect these controls on site.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain methods for supervising cyber-resilience, testing and incident response approaches, and cybersecurity and resilience metrics.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Regulator-led threat-led penetration tests mostly probe a bank's protective and detective capabilities, whereas public-private exercises such as Exercise Resilient Shield rehearse information sharing, incident handling and public communication rather than testing the bank.
cards.explanation: Directed penetration tests focus mainly on protection and detection, and Exercise Resilient Shield was explicitly not a test of individual firms.
cards.originalText: The test will most likely probe the bank’s protective and detective capabilities; the exercise rehearses information sharing, incident handling and public communication rather than testing the bank.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain methods for supervising cyber-resilience, testing and incident response approaches, and cybersecurity and resilience metrics.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Regulator-led penetration tests are typically mandatory for all banks, funded by the supervisor and focused on response and recovery.
cards.explanation: Such tests are typically voluntary, funded by the regulated institution and targeted at larger, more systemic institutions, and they mostly focus on protective and detective capabilities.
cards.originalText: Like most regulator-led penetration tests, the test will be mandatory for all banks, funded by the supervisor and focused on response and recovery.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain methods for supervising cyber-resilience, testing and incident response approaches, and cybersecurity and resilience metrics.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: A public-private cyber exercise such as Exercise Resilient Shield scores each bank individually and places a bank that fails it on a supervisory remediation plan.
cards.explanation: The exercise was explicitly not a test of individual firms, so there is no bank-by-bank score.
cards.originalText: The exercise will be scored bank by bank, and a bank that fails it will be placed on a supervisory remediation plan.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain methods for supervising cyber-resilience, testing and incident response approaches, and cybersecurity and resilience metrics.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: A public-private cyber exercise such as Exercise Resilient Shield includes live play against the bank's systems, so that the responses of law enforcement and intelligence agencies can be tested.
cards.explanation: The exercise was not a cyber war game and included no live play, and it did not test law enforcement or the security and intelligence agencies.
cards.originalText: The exercise will include live play against the bank’s systems, so that the responses of law enforcement and intelligence agencies can be tested.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Where the chief risk officer also acts as chief AML/CFT officer, that officer is responsible for reporting suspicious transactions and is the contact point for supervisors and the financial intelligence unit on AML/CFT issues.
cards.explanation: The Basel Committee guidelines allow the chief AML/CFT officer to also perform the chief risk or chief compliance officer function, with a direct reporting line to senior management or the board.
cards.originalText: In the combined role, the CRO as chief AML/CFT oﬀicer is responsible for reporting suspicious transactions and is the contact point for supervisors and the FIU on AML/CFT issues.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Smurfing, splitting a large cash sum into many small deposits below the reporting threshold, is a layering technique.
cards.explanation: Smurfing is a placement technique, the first stage of money laundering. Layering is the later stage that mixes amounts and patterns to obscure the trail.
cards.originalText: The training module classifies smurfing, splitting a large cash sum into many small deposits below the reporting threshold, as layering, the stage that mixes amounts and patterns.
cards.correction: Smurfing, splitting a large cash sum into many small deposits below the reporting threshold, is a placement technique.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Where a new customer's first deposit comes from her own account at another bank subject to the same CDD standard, a bank may rely on that bank's due diligence instead of conducting its own.
cards.explanation: A matching CDD standard at the other bank gives only comfort. It does not remove the receiving bank's obligation to conduct its own due diligence.
cards.originalText: Where a new customer’s first deposit comes from her own account at another bank subject to the same CDD standard, the bank may rely on that bank’s due diligence instead of its own.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Because every correspondent banking relationship carries the same level of ML/FT risk, a bank should apply identical enhanced due diligence to every respondent bank.
cards.explanation: Not all correspondent banking relationships bear the same level of risk, so due diligence is risk-based rather than uniform.
cards.originalText: Because every correspondent banking relationship carries the same level of ML/FT risk, the manual applies identical enhanced due diligence to every respondent bank.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Confidential numbered accounts must be subject to exactly the same CDD as all other accounts, and the holder's verified identity must be known to enough staff for effective due diligence.
cards.explanation: Numbered accounts must not function as anonymous accounts, even if the procedures are carried out by selected staff.
cards.originalText: Confidential numbered accounts go through exactly the same CDD as all other accounts, and the holder’s verified identity is known to enough staff for effective due diligence.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Customers who cannot attend an interview in person are exempt from identity verification, provided their accounts are placed under closer ongoing monitoring.
cards.explanation: There is no exemption for non-face-to-face customers. Closer monitoring complements verification and does not substitute for it.
cards.originalText: Clients who cannot attend an interview in person are exempt from identity verification, provided their accounts are placed under closer ongoing monitoring.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: For corporate clients, a signed written declaration of the beneficial owner's identity is sufficient verification, with no further evidence required.
cards.explanation: A declaration may be requested but must never be relied on alone. The identity of beneficial owners must be verified with other evidence.
cards.originalText: For corporate clients, a signed written declaration of the beneficial owner’s identity is accepted as suﬀicient verification, with no further evidence sought.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
