cards.originalText: Because the bonds are debt until a trigger event, their holders cannot bear any loss until the bank’s common shareholders have been completely wiped out.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Compare the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) to earlier methods of calculating operational risk capital, including the Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA).
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: In the Basel III standardised approach for operational risk, the 12%, 15% and 18% coefficients vary by business line.
cards.explanation: The Basel III approach has no business-line split. Its coefficients depend on the size bucket of the business indicator.
cards.originalText: In both approaches the percentages vary by business line, but the Basel III approach applies them to the business indicator instead of gross income.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Compare the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) to earlier methods of calculating operational risk capital, including the Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA).
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Like the basic indicator approach, the Basel III standardised approach for operational risk ignores years in which the relevant income items were negative.
cards.explanation: The business indicator uses absolute values of its income items year by year, so a loss-making year still adds to it. The basic indicator approach is the one that ignores negative years.
cards.originalText: Like the basic indicator approach, the Basel III approach ignores years in which the relevant income items were negative.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Compare the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) to earlier methods of calculating operational risk capital, including the Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA).
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: In the Basel II standardized approach (TSA) the 12%, 15% and 18% percentages are betas that vary by business line, whereas in the Basel III standardised approach they are marginal coefficients that rise with the size of the business indicator.
cards.explanation: The TSA applies a beta by business line according to its perceived riskiness. The Basel III approach applies 12% up to EUR 1 billion, 15% from 1 to 30 billion and 18% above 30 billion of the business indicator.
cards.originalText: In the TSA the percentages are betas that vary by business line; in the Basel III approach they are marginal coeﬀicients that rise with the size of the business indicator.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Compare the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) to earlier methods of calculating operational risk capital, including the Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA).
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: In the Basel III standardised approach for operational risk, a bank whose business indicator exceeds EUR 30 billion applies 18% to its whole business indicator.
cards.explanation: The coefficients are marginal: 18% applies only to the part of the business indicator above EUR 30 billion.
cards.originalText: In the Basel III approach a bank whose business indicator exceeds EUR 30 billion applies 18% to its whole business indicator.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Compare the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) to earlier methods of calculating operational risk capital, including the Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA).
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III standardised approach, the loss component is based on the 99.9th percentile of a modelled aggregate loss distribution.
cards.explanation: The loss component is 15 times average annual losses over ten years. No percentile is modelled.
cards.originalText: The LDA remains the Pillar 1 engine: the 99.9th percentile of the aggregate loss distribution now feeds the loss component in place of average losses.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Compare the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) to earlier methods of calculating operational risk capital, including the Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA).
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III standardised approach, banks are prohibited from modelling operational risk losses for any purpose.
cards.explanation: Banks may still model operational risk for Pillar 2, ICAAP and stress testing. Only Pillar 1 capital follows the prescribed formula.
cards.originalText: The LDA is now prohibited, since the standardised approach requires banks to stop modelling operational risk losses for any purpose.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Compare the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) to earlier methods of calculating operational risk capital, including the Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA).
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III standardised approach, only bucket 1 banks may use a loss distribution approach for Pillar 1 capital.
cards.explanation: No bank uses a loss distribution approach for Pillar 1 under the standardised approach. Bucket 1 banks simply have an internal loss multiplier of 1.
cards.originalText: The LDA is now used only by bucket 1 banks, which do not include internal loss data in the standardised approach.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Compare the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) to earlier methods of calculating operational risk capital, including the Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA).
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Under the Basel III standardised approach, a loss distribution approach no longer sets Pillar 1 operational risk capital, which follows a prescribed formula of the business indicator and average past losses, but it can still serve Pillar 2 (ICAAP) capital and stress testing.
cards.explanation: The formula combines the business indicator component with an internal loss multiplier driven by the loss component. Modelling effort is transferred to Pillar 2 and stress testing.
cards.originalText: The LDA no longer sets Pillar 1 capital, which follows a prescribed formula of the business indicator and average past losses; it can still serve Pillar 2 (ICAAP) capital and stress testing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Describe general and specific criteria recommended by the Basel Committee for the identification, collection, and treatment of operational loss data.
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Banks must use the date of discovery as the date for building the standardised approach loss data set.
cards.explanation: Banks must use the date of accounting. The date of discovery is a recorded field but not the date that builds the data set.
cards.originalText: Losses enter the data set on their date of discovery, since that is when the bank becomes aware of the event.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Describe general and specific criteria recommended by the Basel Committee for the identification, collection, and treatment of operational loss data.
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Losses from one event that are posted to the accounts over several years are recorded in full in the year in which the event first occurred.
cards.explanation: Grouped losses are allocated to the corresponding years in line with their accounting treatment, not recorded in the year of occurrence.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Describe general and specific criteria recommended by the Basel Committee for the identification, collection, and treatment of operational loss data.
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: A legal loss enters the standardised approach loss data set no later than the date on which a legal reserve for the probable estimated loss is established in the P&L.
cards.explanation: For legal events, the date of accounting is the date a legal reserve is established for the probable estimated loss. Banks use the date of accounting to build the loss data set.
cards.originalText: A legal loss enters the data set no later than the date on which a legal reserve for the probable estimated loss is established in the P&L.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Describe general and specific criteria recommended by the Basel Committee for the identification, collection, and treatment of operational loss data.
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: An insurance claim is netted against the gross loss as soon as it is lodged, because it is a receivable linked to the event.
cards.explanation: A lodged claim is only a receivable. Recoveries reduce a loss only after payment is received.
cards.originalText: An insurance claim accepted by the insurer is netted against the gross loss as soon as it is lodged, since it is a receivable linked to the event.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Describe general and specific criteria recommended by the Basel Committee for the identification, collection, and treatment of operational loss data.
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: A bank may itself exclude from its loss component any loss that it judges no longer relevant to its risk profile, provided the loss is older than five years.
cards.explanation: Exclusion is a supervisory decision that requires approval, and there is no five-year rule.
cards.originalText: A bank may exclude any loss that it judges no longer relevant to its risk profile, provided the loss is older than five years.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Describe general and specific criteria recommended by the Basel Committee for the identification, collection, and treatment of operational loss data.
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Excluding an operational loss event from the loss component needs supervisory approval and should be rare; the bank must show that the cause could not recur elsewhere in its operations, and exclusions are disclosed under Pillar 3.
cards.explanation: Exclusion requires strong justification, and supervisors consider whether the cause could occur in other areas of the bank. Banks must also show no similar or residual legal exposure.
cards.originalText: Exclusion needs supervisory approval and should be rare; the bank must show the cause could not recur elsewhere in its operations, and exclusions are disclosed under Pillar 3.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Describe general and specific criteria recommended by the Basel Committee for the identification, collection, and treatment of operational loss data.
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Losses from a divested subsidiary can be excluded only after a minimum retention period in the loss database, typically three years.
cards.explanation: Losses related to divested activities are not subject to a minimum retention period in the loss database.
cards.originalText: Losses from the divested subsidiary can be excluded only after a minimum retention period in the loss database, typically three years.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.loText: Describe general and specific criteria recommended by the Basel Committee for the identification, collection, and treatment of operational loss data.
cards.reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
cards.statement: Settled legal losses are excluded from the loss component automatically once paid, since a settled case leaves no residual legal exposure.
cards.explanation: Nothing is excluded automatically. The bank must demonstrate that there is no similar or residual exposure and obtain supervisory approval.
cards.originalText: Settled legal losses are excluded automatically once paid, since a settled case leaves no residual legal exposure.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Risk identification is the step of the risk management cycle that evaluates the likelihood of a risk occurring and its severity if it does occur.
cards.explanation: Identification defines, discovers and categorizes risks. Rating them on likelihood and severity is risk assessment.
cards.originalText: Risk identification.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Risk assessment is the step of the risk management cycle that evaluates the likelihood of a risk occurring and its severity if it does occur.
cards.explanation: Assessment rates each identified risk on likelihood and severity so that risks that are too likely or too severe can be prioritized for mitigation.
cards.originalText: Risk assessment.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Risk mitigation is the step of the risk management cycle that evaluates the likelihood of a risk occurring and its severity if it does occur.
cards.explanation: Mitigation is the response, such as controls, insurance or exposure reduction, applied after assessment. It does not evaluate likelihood and impact.
cards.originalText: Risk mitigation.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Risk monitoring is the step of the risk management cycle that evaluates the likelihood of a risk occurring and its severity if it does occur.
cards.explanation: Monitoring checks that the process works as intended, using KRIs and incident reports, and feeds lessons back into the cycle. It is not the initial rating of risks.
cards.originalText: Risk monitoring.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Credit risk associated with a company's investments in the stock market falls within the scope of an operational risk management framework.
cards.explanation: Investment-related credit risk is a financial risk managed under its own framework, not under operational risk management.
cards.originalText: Credit risk associated with a company’s investments in the stock market.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Firms should develop a holistic picture of their risk management practices that clarifies the relationships between actions, tools and techniques.
cards.explanation: A holistic view linking actions, tools and techniques is recommended for an operational risk management framework.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Regulated financial services companies are required to define their risk appetite and tolerance, which drives the priorities of risk exposure and mitigation.
cards.explanation: Risk appetite is a regulatory requirement for regulated firms and a main component of the operational risk management framework.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Risk governance relates to assigning roles and responsibilities in the organization to execute and report on risk management.
cards.explanation: This is the definition of risk governance within an operational risk management framework.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Risk monitoring focuses on the definition, discovery, selection and categorization of the risks faced by a business.
cards.explanation: Definition, discovery, selection and categorization describe risk identification. Monitoring checks that everything works as intended and tracks the evolution of risks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Scenario analysis and stress testing are most likely used in the risk mitigation step of the risk management process.
cards.explanation: Mitigation uses controls, insurance and exposure reduction, not scenario modeling.
cards.originalText: Risk mitigation.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Scenario analysis and stress testing are most likely used in the risk monitoring step of the risk management process.
cards.explanation: Monitoring uses tools such as incident reports and key risk indicators.
cards.originalText: Risk monitoring.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Scenario analysis and stress testing are most likely used in the risk assessment step of the risk management process.
cards.explanation: Assessment determines the likelihood and severity of identified risks. Scenario analysis and stress testing estimate how severe losses could be under adverse conditions.
cards.originalText: Risk assessment.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Describe an operational risk management framework and assess the types of risks that can fall within the scope of such a framework.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Scenario analysis and stress testing are most likely used in the risk identification step of the risk management process.
cards.explanation: Identification uses tools such as brainstorming, interviews and loss logs to list risks. It does not size them.
cards.originalText: Risk identification.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Heterogeneity means that operational risk is highly varied because it encompasses diverse risks, such as fraud in retail transactions and damage to physical assets.
cards.explanation: Operational risk is an eclectic set of risks with different causes, consequences and loss distributions.
cards.originalText: Heterogeneous ‑ operational risk is highly varied because it encompasses diverse risks, such as fraud in retail transactions and damage to physical assets

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational risk is idiosyncratic and diffuse in the sense that the distribution of operational losses is highly skewed, with most of the density concentrated in the lowest part of the distribution.
cards.explanation: A highly skewed loss distribution, with many small losses and few huge ones, describes the heavy-tailed characteristic.
cards.originalText: Idiosyncratic and diffuse ‑ the distribution of operational losses is highly skewed, with most of the density concentrated in the lowest part of the distribution

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational risk is interconnected in the sense that it arises from every person and process in the firm, so everyone has to take part in managing it.
cards.explanation: Risk arising from every person and process and managed by everyone describes the idiosyncratic and diffuse characteristic. Interconnected means correlated risks and boundary events.
cards.originalText: Interconnected ‑ operational risk arises from every person and process in the firm, so everyone has to take part in managing it

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational risk is heavy-tailed in the sense that it evolves with the activities and development of the industry.
cards.explanation: Evolving with the industry describes the dynamic characteristic. Heavy-tailed refers to a skewed loss distribution with rare, very large losses.
cards.originalText: Heavy‑tailed ‑ operational risk evolves with the activities and development of the industry

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: A high-beta firm can lower its beta most easily by centralizing its operational risk management function.
cards.explanation: Beta captures market co-movement, while operational risk is idiosyncratic and diffuse and cannot be centralized in the way market or credit risk management can.
cards.originalText: The easiest way for a high‑beta firm to lower its beta is to centralize the ORM function.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational risk is highly homogeneous because boundary events define clusters of loss events with shared features.
cards.explanation: Operational risk is heterogeneous. Boundary events begin in one risk category and materialize in another, which shows interconnectedness, not homogeneity.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Most causes of operational risk trace to control weaknesses, human biases and behavioral failings, and/or changes in the operating environment.
cards.explanation: These are the common root causes of operational risk events, and they also underlie other types of risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational risk is described as dynamic because it cannot be fully eliminated through traditional methods such as hedging.
cards.explanation: Dynamic means that exposures evolve with business practices, which makes modeling hard. Irreducibility is the idiosyncratic characteristic.
cards.originalText: Dynamic.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: The idiosyncratic nature of operational risk means that avoidance, hedging or insurance can reduce it but never fully eliminate it, leaving residual exposure.
cards.explanation: Operational risk is driven by a firm's own people, processes and systems and cannot be centralized or hedged away, so some residual risk always remains.
cards.originalText: Idiosyncratic.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational risk is described as heterogeneous because it cannot be fully eliminated through traditional methods such as hedging.
cards.explanation: Heterogeneous means that operational risk consists of diverse risks with different causes and loss distributions, which complicates classification.
cards.originalText: Heterogeneous.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.loText: Explain characteristics of operational risk exposures and operational loss events, and challenges that can arise in managing operational risk due to these characteristics.
cards.reading: ORR-1: Introduction to Operational Risk and Resilience
cards.statement: Operational risk is described as interconnected because it cannot be fully eliminated through traditional methods such as hedging.
cards.explanation: Interconnected means that operational risks are correlated and that boundary events overlap with market and credit risk, not that residual risk remains after hedging.
cards.originalText: Interconnected.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under Principle 3 of the Basel Committee's Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk, the board is responsible for approving the operational risk management framework (ORMF).
cards.explanation: Approving the ORMF is a core board duty under Principle 3.
cards.originalText: Validating (approving) the operational risk management framework (ORMF).

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under Principle 3 of the Basel Committee's Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk, the board is responsible for ensuring that the ORMF is revised periodically.
cards.explanation: Periodic revision of the ORMF is a stated board responsibility.
cards.originalText: Ensuring the ORMF is revised periodically.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under Principle 3 of the Basel Committee's Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk, the board is responsible for obtaining assurance that senior management implements the ORMF policies, processes and systems effectively at all levels of the bank.
cards.explanation: Obtaining assurance that senior management implements the framework is a board oversight duty.
cards.originalText: Obtaining assurance that senior management implements the ORMF policies, processes, and systems effectively at all levels of the bank.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The board is responsible for designing and maintaining the day-to-day operational risk procedures and control systems used by the business lines.
cards.explanation: The board approves, reviews and oversees. Designing and running the procedures and controls is implementation work done by senior management, the first line and the corporate operational risk function.
cards.originalText: Designing and maintaining the day‑to‑day operational risk procedures and control systems used by the business lines.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The purpose of risk governance within an operational risk management framework is to replace Pillar 1 regulatory capital with qualitative controls over operational risk.
cards.explanation: Operational risk management is balanced with, not a substitute for, regulatory capital. Governance does not replace Pillar 1 capital.
cards.originalText: To replace Pillar 1 regulatory capital with qualitative controls over operational risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The purpose of risk governance within an operational risk management framework is to develop robust governance policies and processes and manage material risks in line with the firm's risk appetite.
cards.explanation: Governance puts in place the policies, processes and committee structure that keep material operational risks within the board-approved risk appetite.
cards.originalText: To develop robust governance policies and processes and manage material risks in line with the firm’s risk appetite.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The purpose of risk governance within an operational risk management framework is to shift responsibility for operational risk decisions from the bank to its supervisors.
cards.explanation: Supervisors review the framework under Pillar 2, but accountability remains with the bank's board and management.
cards.originalText: To shift responsibility for operational risk decisions from the bank to its supervisors.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The purpose of risk governance within an operational risk management framework is to restrict operational risk management to the second line of defense, so that the business lines carry no risk responsibility.
cards.explanation: Under the three-lines model, the first line owns risk and the second line only oversees and challenges.
cards.originalText: To restrict operational risk management to the second line of defense so that the business lines carry no risk responsibility.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: One way to examine whether an operational risk management framework is being implemented is to ask whether there is evidence that all material events are captured in event reports.
cards.explanation: Incident reports should account for all significant incidents, so completeness of event reporting is a valid implementation check.
cards.originalText: Is there evidence that all material events are captured in event reports?

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: One way to examine whether an operational risk management framework is being implemented is to ask whether the value of each risk indicator comes from an independent source.
cards.explanation: Risk indicators should be computed objectively and without bias, so independence of their source is a valid implementation check.
cards.originalText: Does the value of each risk indicator come from an independent source?

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: One way to examine whether an operational risk management framework is being implemented is to ask whether the presented data are sufficient for decision-making.
cards.explanation: Regulators ask whether reports give enough information for proper decisions, so this is a valid implementation check.
cards.originalText: Are the presented data sufficient for decision‑making?

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under Principle 3 of the Basel Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk, the board should ensure that the operational risk management framework is subject to independent review by sufficiently skilled personnel.
cards.explanation: Principle 3 concerns the board's review and approval of the operational risk management framework itself, including independent review of it.
cards.originalText: Ensure the ORM framework is subject to independent review by sufficiently skilled personnel.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under Principle 3 of the Basel Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk, the board identifies the types and levels of operational risk the bank is willing to assume and approves the risk appetite and risk tolerance statements.
cards.explanation: Setting and approving risk appetite and tolerance statements is covered by Principle 4, while Principle 3 concerns the board's approval and review of the operational risk management framework.
cards.originalText: Identify the types and levels of operational risk the bank is willing to assume, and approve risk appetite and risk tolerance statements.
cards.correction: Under Principle 4 of the Basel Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk, the board identifies the types and levels of operational risk the bank is willing to assume and approves the risk appetite and risk tolerance statements.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: To maintain independence, the operational risk management framework prohibits any reporting relationship, even dotted-line, from the corporate operational risk management function to either the Chief Risk Officer or the board's risk committee.
cards.explanation: Independence of the corporate operational risk management function is from the business units that generate risk, so it can and does report to the Chief Risk Officer and the board risk committee.
cards.originalText: To maintain independence, the ORMF prohibits any reporting relationship (even dotted‑line) from the CORF to either the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) or the board’s risk committee.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The operational risk management framework should provide for a common taxonomy of operational risk terms to ensure consistency of risk identification, exposure rating and risk management objectives.
cards.explanation: A common taxonomy, for example of loss event types, supports consistent identification and rating of operational risk.
cards.originalText: The ORMF should provide for a common taxonomy of operational risk terms to ensure consistency of risk identification (e.g., operational loss event types), exposure rating, and risk management objectives.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Compensation plans should be aligned with the bank's risk appetite and risk tolerance, and may include incentive pay explicitly linked to risk-adjusted measures, deferral mechanisms or claw-backs.
cards.explanation: Pay is expected to be consistent with appetite and tolerance, using tools such as risk-adjusted incentives, deferral and claw-backs.
cards.originalText: Compensation plans should be aligned with the bank’s risk appetite and risk tolerance; such plans may include incentive compensation explicitly linked to risk‑adjusted measures, deferral mechanisms, or claw‑backs.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The board of directors approves a risk appetite statement, a forward-looking high-level view of risk acceptance that incorporates return expectations, and a risk tolerance statement, a more specific determination of the level of variation the bank is willing to accept around business objectives, for operational risk.
cards.explanation: Appetite is high level and forward looking, while tolerance is more specific about the variation the bank will accept, and the board approves both.
cards.originalText: The board of directors approves a risk appetite statement (a forward‑looking, high‑level view of risk acceptance that incorporates return expectations) and a risk tolerance statement (a more specific determination of the level of variation the bank is willing to accept around business objectives) for operational risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Basel governance expectations for operational risk include an independent review of the bank's operational risk management framework.
cards.explanation: Independent review of the operational risk management framework is a core governance expectation, alongside board validation and periodic revision of the framework.
cards.originalText: Require an independent review of the bank’s operational risk management framework.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Third-party outsourcing agreements can replace most of the internal controls performed by senior managers and business line managers.
cards.explanation: Outsourcing may complement internal controls but cannot replace them, and accountability for the controls remains with the bank.
cards.originalText: Use third‑party outsourcing agreements to replace most internal controls performed by senior managers and business line managers.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: Under the Basel III standardised approach, a bank determines its operational risk regulatory capital using its own internal model of the distribution of operational risk losses.
cards.explanation: The standardised approach replaced internal modelling with a single formula-based measure, operational risk capital = business indicator component x internal loss multiplier.
cards.originalText: Develop an internal approach to model the distribution of operational risk losses and use it to determine the bank’s regulatory capital.
cards.correction: Under the Basel III standardised approach, a bank determines its operational risk regulatory capital using a single formula based on the business indicator component and the internal loss multiplier.

changes.from: its own internal model of the distribution of operational risk losses
changes.to: a single formula based on the business indicator component and the internal loss multiplier

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.loText: Explain the Basel regulatory expectations for the governance of an operational risk management framework.
cards.reading: ORR-2: Risk Governance
cards.statement: The risk management function is the primary owner of risk exposures within each business line.
cards.explanation: Risk is owned by the business itself, the first line of defense, while the risk management function is the second line that oversees and challenges.
cards.originalText: Designate the risk management function as the primary owner of risk exposures within each business line.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Top-down risk identification begins at the executive level, then moves to the business units and finally to individual business processes.
cards.explanation: Top-down identification starts with the board and senior management and cascades through divisions or business units down to business processes.
cards.originalText: Top‑down risk identification

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Bottom-up risk identification begins at the executive level, then moves to the business units and finally to individual business processes.
cards.explanation: Bottom-up identification starts with business units, staff and processes and works upward; the executive-to-process sequence describes top-down identification.
cards.originalText: Bottom‑up risk identification
cards.correction: Top-down risk identification begins at the executive level, then moves to the business units and finally to individual business processes.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Process mapping is a top-down risk identification tool.
cards.explanation: Process mapping walks through the steps of a specific process to find what could go wrong, which makes it a detailed bottom-up tool.
cards.originalText: Process mapping
cards.correction: Process mapping is a bottom-up risk identification tool.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Exposures and vulnerabilities is a top-down risk identification tool.
cards.explanation: Senior management lists the firm's significant exposures and weak spots, which is a top-down exercise.
cards.originalText: Exposures and vulnerabilities

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: The risk wheel is a top-down risk identification tool.
cards.explanation: The risk wheel is a top-down brainstorming tool that shows causal links between risk types.
cards.originalText: Risk wheel

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Horizon scanning is a top-down risk identification tool.
cards.explanation: Horizon scanning is a top-down tool for identifying emerging risks and can be structured with a PESTLE analysis.
cards.originalText: Horizon scanning

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Systems overdue for updates are classified as an exposure under top-down risk identification tools.
cards.explanation: Systems overdue for updates are a weakness in the firm, which makes them a vulnerability rather than an exposure.
cards.originalText: Systems overdue for updates
cards.correction: Systems overdue for updates are classified as a vulnerability under top-down risk identification tools.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Critical third parties are classified as exposures under top-down risk identification tools.
cards.explanation: Exposures are areas of business dependence where a failure would have a large impact, and dependence on critical third parties through outsourcing is a typical example.
cards.originalText: Critical third parties

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: The main drivers of revenues are classified as exposures under top-down risk identification tools.
cards.explanation: Main revenue drivers are areas of business dependence, so they are listed as exposures.
cards.originalText: Main drivers of revenues

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Near misses are incidents that could have resulted in operational losses but did not, because of interventions outside the normal course of controls.
cards.explanation: A near miss is an incident that could have caused a loss but was prevented by luck or an intervention outside normal controls, and analysing near misses is a bottom-up risk identification tool.
cards.originalText: Near misses

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Horizon scanning is a top-down approach to risk identification that can be carried out in a structured way with a PESTLE analysis.
cards.explanation: Horizon scanning identifies emerging risks from the top down, and PESTLE (political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental) gives it structure.
cards.originalText: Horizon scanning is a top‑down approach that might be achieved in a structured way with a PESTLE analysis

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Because bottom-up tools only identify risks that have already occurred, their chief drawback is a tendency to overlook non-financial risks such as reputational or compliance risk.
cards.explanation: Bottom-up tools such as risk and control self-assessment also look at potential future risks and cover non-financial risks, so they are not limited to past events.
cards.originalText: Because bottom‑up tools only identify risks that have already occurred (rather than potential future risks), their chief drawback is a tendency to overlook non‑financial risks such as reputational or compliance

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A bank should choose between a top-down and a bottom-up approach to risk identification in order to avoid confusing those in the middle of the organization.
cards.explanation: The two approaches are complementary and are combined to give a fuller picture of risk, not chosen between.
cards.originalText: The bank should choose between either a top‑down or bottom‑up approach to risk identification in order to avoid confusing those in the middle of the organization

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: The risk wheel should be avoided because it is a novelty and gamification tends to distract from the seriousness of the exercise.
cards.explanation: The risk wheel is a valued brainstorming tool that encourages creativity and shows cause-and-effect chains between risks.
cards.originalText: Although popular in the 80s and 90s, the risk wheel should be avoided because it is a novelty, and gamification tends to distract from the seriousness of the exercise

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Large company projects are a typical example of an exposure in top-down risk identification.
cards.explanation: Exposures are significant areas of business dependence where a failure would have a large impact, such as large projects, critical third parties and key clients.
cards.originalText: Large company projects.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Outdated processes are classified as an exposure in top-down risk identification.
cards.explanation: Outdated processes are a weakness in how the firm operates, so they are a vulnerability rather than an exposure.
cards.originalText: Outdated processes.
cards.correction: Outdated processes are classified as a vulnerability in top-down risk identification.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Stand-alone IT systems are a typical example of a vulnerability in risk identification.
cards.explanation: Vulnerabilities are the firm's weakest links, and stand-alone systems are often poorly monitored or updated.
cards.originalText: Stand‑alone IT systems.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: The principal regulator is a typical example of a vulnerability in risk identification.
cards.explanation: The principal regulator is a dependency, since regulatory reporting and fines can be costly, so it is an exposure rather than a vulnerability.
cards.originalText: Principal regulator.
cards.correction: The principal regulator is a typical example of an exposure in risk identification.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Critical third parties are a typical example of a vulnerability in risk identification.
cards.explanation: Dependence on critical third parties through outsourcing is an exposure, not a weak spot in the firm's own operations.
cards.originalText: Critical third parties.
cards.correction: Critical third parties are a typical example of an exposure in risk identification.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A Chief Risk Officer who prefers to assess operational risk at a local and detailed level should recommend the risk wheel.
cards.explanation: The risk wheel is a senior-level, top-down brainstorming tool, which is inconsistent with a local, detailed focus.
cards.originalText: Risk wheel.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Process mapping is a bottom-up, process-specific risk identification tool suited to assessing operational risk at a local and detailed level.
cards.explanation: Process mapping examines the steps of individual processes, so it fits a local, detailed assessment.
cards.originalText: Process mapping.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Risk and control self-assessment is performed by business units, which makes it a bottom-up tool suited to local, detailed assessment of operational risk.
cards.explanation: Business units carry out the assessment of their own risks and controls, so it is a bottom-up approach.
cards.originalText: Risk and control self‑assessment.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A risk register combines the inventory of a firm's operational risks with the controls applied to each risk and an assessment of each risk's residual likelihood and impact.
cards.explanation: The risk register is the central repository of operational risks with their controls and residual likelihood and impact.
cards.originalText: Risk register

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Horizon scanning is used in the risk identification activity of an operational risk management framework.
cards.explanation: Horizon scanning is a top-down tool for spotting emerging risks, which is a risk identification activity.
cards.originalText: Risk identification.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Horizon scanning is used in the risk assessment activity of an operational risk management framework.
cards.explanation: Risk assessment measures the likelihood and impact of risks that have already been identified, whereas horizon scanning looks ahead to find emerging risks, which is risk identification.
cards.originalText: Risk assessment.
cards.correction: Horizon scanning is used in the risk identification activity of an operational risk management framework.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: The labor market is one of the six components of PESTLE used for scanning horizon risks.
cards.explanation: PESTLE has exactly six components, Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental, and labor market is not one of them.
cards.originalText: Labor market component

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Political is one of the six components of PESTLE used for scanning horizon risks.
cards.explanation: The P in PESTLE stands for Political; the others are Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental.
cards.originalText: Political component

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Discuss different top-down and bottom-up approaches and tools for identifying operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Emerging risks are nascent risks that are relatively small today but on the rise, with the potential for significant impact in the future.
cards.explanation: Emerging risks are found through horizon scanning rather than from existing risk lists.
cards.originalText: Emerging risks

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: An external expert invited to a scenario analysis workshop can help mitigate myopia, the undue emphasis on recent events.
cards.explanation: An outsider is not anchored by the firm's recent experience and can widen the range of scenarios considered.
cards.originalText: Myopia, the undue emphasis on recent events

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: A common bias in scenario analysis is an excessive focus on scenarios driven by internal causes rather than external ones.
cards.explanation: The documented bias is an excessive focus on external causes, while internal causes such as rogue trading, misselling and IT failures are underweighted.
cards.originalText: An excessive focus on scenarios driven by internal causes
cards.correction: A common bias in scenario analysis is an excessive focus on scenarios driven by external causes rather than internal ones.

changes.from: internal causes rather than external ones
changes.to: external causes rather than internal ones

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Myopia in scenario analysis is an underestimation of the impact of recent events.
cards.explanation: Myopia is an over-emphasis on recent events, so it leads to overestimating their importance.
cards.originalText: Underestimation of the impact of recent events
cards.correction: Myopia in scenario analysis is an overestimation of the impact of recent events.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Reliance on empirical evidence to support scenario assumptions is itself a bias in scenario analysis.
cards.explanation: Basing assumptions on empirical evidence is expected by regulators to reduce subjectivity, so it is a safeguard rather than a bias.
cards.originalText: Reliance on empirical evidence to support scenario assumptions

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Good practice in scenario analysis is to compare the firm's own generated scenarios with industry-specific lists published by external sources, but only after the firm's own internal generation exercise.
cards.explanation: Delaying the external comparison avoids anchoring on the external list while still checking the firm's own list for gaps.
cards.originalText: She should compare her firm’s generated scenarios to industry‑specific list(s) published by external sources, but only after her firm’s own internal generation exercise.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Because most large operational losses result from external causes, the primary focus of scenario analysis should be scenarios driven by external causes.
cards.explanation: Large losses often have internal causes, and focusing mainly on external causes is a bias to be avoided.
cards.originalText: Because most large operational losses result from external causes, her primary focus should be scenarios driven by external causes.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Because the ultimate goal of scenario analysis is to predict the future with a sufficient degree of certainty, the process should acknowledge and elevate the role of human subjectivity.
cards.explanation: Scenario analysis aims at plausible severe outcomes and repeatable results, and regulators want subjectivity minimized, not elevated.
cards.originalText: Because the ultimate goal of scenario analysis is to predict the future with a sufficient degree of certainty, her process should acknowledge and elevate the role of human subjectivity.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Large international banks generate fewer scenarios than small firms because their processes are more centralized.
cards.explanation: The number of scenarios rises with firm size and complexity, so larger banks have more scenarios, not fewer.
cards.originalText: Large international banks generate fewer scenarios than small firms because their processes are more centralized.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Scenarios with the same internal impact but different external causes, such as damage to physical assets from weather or from civil unrest, can be consolidated into one scenario.
cards.explanation: Consolidating scenarios by common impact is standard practice in the selection phase.
cards.originalText: Scenarios with the same internal impact but different external causes, such as damage to physical assets from weather or from civil unrest, can be consolidated into one scenario.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: In the selection phase of scenario analysis, scenarios whose maximum likely loss is small enough to be absorbed by the normal operating margin can be eliminated before assessment.
cards.explanation: Scenarios with a moderate, absorbable maximum loss are removed at selection so that effort is spent on the severe ones.
cards.originalText: Scenarios whose maximum likely loss is small enough to be absorbed by normal operating margin can be eliminated before assessment.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: The initial output of scenario identification should contain at least 20 to 30 scenarios for a mid-size firm, with roughly 15 remaining after selection.
cards.explanation: Scenario identification starts broad and the selection phase narrows the list.
cards.originalText: The initial output of scenario identification should contain at least 20 to 30 scenarios for a mid‑size firm, with roughly 15 remaining after selection.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Consolidating two scenarios in which different external events cause the same impact on the bank's infrastructure into a single scenario is consistent with best practice in scenario selection.
cards.explanation: Consolidating scenarios by common impact is explicitly endorsed in the selection phase.
cards.originalText: Participants consolidated two scenarios in which different external events caused the same impact on the bank’s infrastructure into a single scenario.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Best practice is to begin a scenario workshop by reviewing a set of scenarios from an external industry source and to use them as a guide for generating the firm's scenarios.
cards.explanation: Starting from an external list anchors the participants, so it should be used only after generation as a completeness check.
cards.originalText: Participants began the workshop by reviewing a set of scenarios provided by an external industry source and used these as a guide to generate the scenarios discussed in the workshop.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Assigning a high probability to a severe new pandemic because one occurred in the previous year is consistent with best practice in scenario analysis.
cards.explanation: Overweighting a recent event is the myopia bias, which scenario analysis should guard against.
cards.originalText: Participants assigned a high probability to the occurrence of a severe new pandemic in the future given that one had occurred in the previous year.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Emphasising scenarios arising from external causes, such as geopolitical crises and cyber-attacks, because losses from internal causes are considered unlikely is consistent with best practice in scenario analysis.
cards.explanation: Excessive focus on external causes is a known bias, since internal causes such as rogue trading, misselling and IT failures produce many large losses.
cards.originalText: Participants emphasized scenarios arising from external causes, such as geopolitical crises and cyber‑attacks, as losses from internal causes were considered to be unlikely.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: In scenario identification, having each participant write down their main concerns individually and in silence before any group discussion gives every participant an equal voice and limits dominance by senior participants and anchoring.
cards.explanation: Silent written contributions before discussion prevent a dominant individual from setting the agenda.
cards.originalText: Having each participant write down their main concerns individually and in silence before any group discussion begins.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Asking the most experienced participant to present an initial scenario for the group to refine is an appropriate way to limit seniority dominance and anchoring in a scenario workshop.
cards.explanation: This approach maximizes both seniority dominance and anchoring, because the group refines one person's starting point instead of contributing independently.
cards.originalText: Asking the most experienced participant to present an initial scenario for the group to refine.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: To meet regulators' requirements to minimize subjectivity and bias, scenario assumptions must be based on empirical evidence and their rationale documented.
cards.explanation: Empirical grounding and documentation make scenario results repeatable and neutral, as regulators demand.
cards.originalText: To meet regulators’ requirements to minimize subjectivity and bias, scenario assumptions must be based on empirical evidence and their rationale documented.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: The facilitators of scenario analysis workshops should be drawn from the board of directors and senior management.
cards.explanation: Facilitators are usually operational risk management professionals, not board members.
cards.originalText: The facilitators of the workshops should be drawn from the board of directors and senior management.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Participants in scenario analysis workshops should be drawn from a full range of seniority levels, including junior staff, in each business unit.
cards.explanation: Participants are normally senior managers with experience in their area, not a full range of seniority.
cards.originalText: Participants should be drawn from a full range of seniority levels, including junior staff, in each business unit.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe best practices in extreme risk identification for operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: The most common procedure in scenario analysis workshops is to withhold the preparation pack from participants and distribute it after the generation phase.
cards.explanation: Distributing the preparation pack before the first meetings is the more common practice, and withholding it is only occasional.
cards.originalText: The most common procedure is to withhold the preparation pack from participants and distribute it after the generation phase.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply an operational risk taxonomy and give examples of different taxonomies of operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: In an operational risk taxonomy, impacts include people, external fraud, internal fraud, physical security and safety, business continuity, transaction processing and execution, technology, conduct, legal, financial crime and regulatory compliance.
cards.explanation: That list describes Level 1 risk event types, which map closely to the Basel event types; impacts are classified as direct financial, indirect financial and non-financial.
cards.originalText: Impacts include people, external fraud, internal fraud, physical security & safety, business continuity, transaction processing & execution, technology, conduct, legal, financial crime, and regulatory compliance

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply an operational risk taxonomy and give examples of different taxonomies of operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: In the ORX operational risk taxonomy, causes include people, processes, systems and external events.
cards.explanation: These four categories, abbreviated PPSE, make up the cause taxonomy.
cards.originalText: Causes include people, processes, systems, and external events (aka, PPSE)

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply an operational risk taxonomy and give examples of different taxonomies of operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: Operational risk controls are classified as preventative, detective, corrective or directive.
cards.explanation: Corrective controls mitigate impact, and directive controls are those such as policies, training and instructions.
cards.originalText: Controls are preventative, detective, corrective (i.e., to mitigate impact), or directive

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply an operational risk taxonomy and give examples of different taxonomies of operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: In a risk register, an adverse occurrence such as errors in the valuation of funds is recorded as a risk event, while the manual processing that gives rise to it is recorded as a cause.
cards.explanation: A risk event is a concrete adverse occurrence, whereas causes, impacts and controls are recorded separately in their own taxonomies.
cards.originalText: Errors in the valuation of funds that arise from manual processing of valuation inputs.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.loText: Describe and apply an operational risk taxonomy and give examples of different taxonomies of operational risks.
cards.reading: ORR-3: Risk Identification
cards.statement: An obligation to comply with newly issued operational resilience regulations is a risk event rather than a constraint of the operating environment.
