cards.explanation: It covers governance, policies, systems and risk transfer arrangements. The other two types are historical losses and the business indicator with its subcomponents.
cards.originalText: Qualitative information on operational risk management

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Historical losses are one of the three types of operational risk information that Pillar 3 requires banks to disclose.
cards.explanation: Banks disclose 10 years of aggregate operational losses.
cards.originalText: Historical losses

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: The business indicator and its subcomponents are one of the three types of operational risk information that Pillar 3 requires banks to disclose.
cards.explanation: The business indicator is the primary input to the operational risk capital calculation.
cards.originalText: Business indicator and subcomponents

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Qualitative information on operational risk management is the Pillar 3 disclosure type that presents an entity's governance and risk management structures.
cards.explanation: It describes the arrangements used to manage, mitigate or transfer operational risk, the structure of the risk management and control function, and the policies and procedures in place.
cards.originalText: Qualitative information on operational risk management

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Historical losses are the Pillar 3 operational risk disclosure type that presents an entity's governance and risk management structures.
cards.explanation: Historical losses are quantitative, consisting of 10 years of aggregate losses. Governance and risk management structures are described in the qualitative disclosure.
cards.originalText: Historical losses

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: The business indicator and its subcomponents are the Pillar 3 operational risk disclosure type that presents an entity's governance and risk management structures.
cards.explanation: The business indicator and its subcomponents are quantitative inputs to the capital calculation. Governance and risk management structures are described in the qualitative disclosure.
cards.originalText: Business indicators and subcomponents

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Basel operational risk disclosure requires historical loss data covering a minimum of 3 years of aggregate operational losses.
cards.explanation: Pillar 3 requires 10 years of aggregate operational losses. A 3-year period applies only to some business indicator component data.
cards.originalText: historical loss data covering a minimum of 3 years of aggregate operational losses.
cards.correction: Basel operational risk disclosure requires historical loss data covering a minimum of 10 years of aggregate operational losses.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Basel operational risk disclosure includes the arrangements the bank has in place to transfer operational risks.
cards.explanation: Risk transfer arrangements form part of the required qualitative information on operational risk management.
cards.originalText: arrangements the bank has in place to transfer operational risks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Basel operational risk disclosure includes information on the systems and data used to measure operational risk.
cards.explanation: The systems and data used to measure operational risk are explicitly part of the qualitative disclosure.
cards.originalText: information on systems and data used to measure operational risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Basel operational risk disclosure includes narratives covering the key drivers of operational risk capital calculations.
cards.explanation: Narratives on key drivers and significant changes accompany the quantitative data.
cards.originalText: narratives covering key drivers of operational risk capital calculations.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Functional is one of the criteria under which significant operational risk event triggers are categorized.
cards.explanation: The four trigger criteria for notifying regulators are materiality, reputation, resilience and stability. Functional is not one of them.
cards.originalText: functional.
cards.correction: Resilience is one of the criteria under which significant operational risk event triggers are categorized.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Stability is one of the criteria under which significant operational risk event triggers are categorized.
cards.explanation: Stability covers events that could have serious consequences for the financial system.
cards.originalText: stability.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Materiality is one of the criteria under which significant operational risk event triggers are categorized.
cards.explanation: Materiality covers events that are significant relative to a loss or materiality threshold.
cards.originalText: materiality.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.loText: Explain best practices for reporting risk exposures to regulators and external stakeholders.
cards.reading: ORR-6: Risk Reporting
cards.statement: Reputation is one of the criteria under which significant operational risk event triggers are categorized.
cards.explanation: Reputation covers events that significantly affect the firm's reputation.
cards.originalText: reputation.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In the three lines of defense model, the first line, business line staff and management, owns and manages risk day to day, with decision-making authority and accountability, within the limits set by the risk appetite.
cards.explanation: The first line holds the risk and acts as designated risk owner. Oversight is the second line, and independent assurance reporting to the board is the third line.
cards.originalText: Business line staff and management own and manage risk day to day, with decision‑making authority and accountability, within the limits set by the risk appetite.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Within an enterprise risk management framework, risk culture and corporate culture are independent and should be managed separately.
cards.explanation: Risk culture cannot be separated from corporate culture, because both reflect the same shared values, beliefs and behaviors.
cards.originalText: risk culture and corporate culture are independent and should be managed separately.
cards.correction: Within an enterprise risk management framework, risk culture and corporate culture are inseparable.

changes.from: are independent and should be managed separately

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In an enterprise risk management framework, risk governance incorporates three to four standard lines of defense.
cards.explanation: There are three internal lines of defense, and external audit is often regarded as a fourth.
cards.originalText: risk governance incorporates three to four standard lines of defense.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In an enterprise risk management framework, risk appetite may drive decisions that can lead to refining desired objectives.
cards.explanation: Risk appetite and objectives interact: how much risk the firm will tolerate can feed back into the objectives it pursues.
cards.originalText: risk appetite may drive decisions that can lead to refining desired objectives.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In an enterprise risk management framework, reporting and monitoring are continuous because exposures to risk are constantly changing.
cards.explanation: Exposures change over time, so risk must be monitored and reported on an ongoing basis.
cards.originalText: reporting and monitoring are continuous due to constantly changing exposures to risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: An external auditor is often regarded as a fourth line of defense, sitting outside the three internal lines of defense.
cards.explanation: The first line is business management, the second is risk oversight and the third is internal audit. External audit adds an extra layer of verification beyond these.
cards.originalText: Fourth.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In an enterprise risk management framework, governance sets the roles of the three lines of defense and reporting committees, culture reflects the behaviors and values around managing risk, and appetite defines the level of risk the firm is willing to tolerate.
cards.explanation: Each of the three elements has a distinct function: governance assigns roles, culture shapes behavior, and appetite sets how much risk is tolerated.
cards.originalText: Governance sets the roles of the three lines of defense and reporting committees, culture reflects the behaviors and values around managing risk, and appetite defines the level of risk the firm is willing to tolerate.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In an enterprise risk management framework, governance defines the level of risk the firm is willing to tolerate, culture assigns the three lines of defense, and appetite reflects employee behaviors and values.
cards.explanation: The functions are swapped. Governance assigns the roles of the lines of defense, culture reflects behaviors and values, and appetite defines the level of risk the firm will tolerate.
cards.originalText: Governance defines the level of risk the firm is willing to tolerate, culture assigns the three lines of defense, and appetite reflects employee behaviors and values.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Risk appetite in an enterprise risk management framework applies only to credit and market risk.
cards.explanation: Risk appetite also covers other risks such as liquidity and operational risk.
cards.originalText: Risk appetite applies only to credit and market risk, whereas governance and culture apply to operational risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the role of risk governance, risk appetite, and risk culture in the context of an enterprise risk management (ERM) framework.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Risk culture is determined solely by the second line of defense, so governance and appetite do not influence it.
cards.explanation: Risk culture is a firm-wide trait that involves executives, leadership and employees, and is not owned by one line. Governance and appetite both interact with it.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the elements of a sound stress-testing framework for financial institutions and explain best practices for stress testing.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Reverse stress testing applies mostly qualitative methods, targets immeasurable risks, and tries to identify the circumstances that might cause a firm to fail.
cards.explanation: Reverse stress testing starts from a specific failure outcome and works backward to the circumstances that could produce it.
cards.originalText: Reverse stress testing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the elements of a sound stress-testing framework for financial institutions and explain best practices for stress testing.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Macroeconomic stress testing starts from a specific institutional failure and works backward to identify the circumstances that could cause it.
cards.explanation: Macroeconomic stress testing runs forward from regulator-supplied macroeconomic shocks such as GDP, unemployment and inflation. Working backward from failure is the defining feature of reverse stress testing.
cards.originalText: Macroeconomic stress testing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the elements of a sound stress-testing framework for financial institutions and explain best practices for stress testing.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Reverse stress testing takes an institution-specific adverse outcome, such as the loss of a major client, credit rating downgrades or significant portfolio losses, as its starting point and works backward to the causes.
cards.explanation: Reverse stress testing begins from a specific failure outcome and identifies the circumstances that could lead to it.
cards.originalText: Reverse stress testing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the elements of a sound stress-testing framework for financial institutions and explain best practices for stress testing.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Macroeconomic stress testing starts from institution-specific shocks such as the loss of a major client, credit rating downgrades and significant portfolio losses.
cards.explanation: Macroeconomic stress testing starts from macroeconomic shocks such as changes in GDP, unemployment and inflation. Institution-specific adverse outcomes are the starting point of reverse stress testing.
cards.originalText: Macroeconomic stress testing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the elements of a sound stress-testing framework for financial institutions and explain best practices for stress testing.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Reverse stress testing starts from a specific failure outcome, such as the loss of a licence or massive cyber losses, and works backward to identify the circumstances that could cause it.
cards.explanation: Working backward from a defined failure outcome is the defining feature of reverse stress testing.
cards.originalText: Analyst 2 only.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the elements of a sound stress-testing framework for financial institutions and explain best practices for stress testing.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Macroeconomic stress testing assesses potential changes in the dependencies between measurable and immeasurable risks faced by a bank under adverse economic conditions.
cards.explanation: Macroeconomic stress testing takes the most holistic view of risk, covering both measurable and immeasurable risks and the dependencies between them.
cards.originalText: Assessing potential changes in dependencies between different measurable and immeasurable risks faced by the bank under adverse economic conditions.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Describe the elements of a sound stress-testing framework for financial institutions and explain best practices for stress testing.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Determining how severe a financial market crisis would need to be to result in a bank's insolvency is macroeconomic stress testing.
cards.explanation: This starts from a defined failure outcome and works backward, which is reverse stress testing.
cards.originalText: Determining how severe a financial market crisis would need to be in order to result in the bank’s insolvency.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: A standard loss distribution approach has no risk drivers and assumes the firm's risk exposure is unchanged over time, so it cannot show how losses respond to a changing macroeconomic environment.
cards.explanation: Stress testing aims to show how exposure changes with the macroeconomic environment, but a standard loss distribution approach treats a higher observed loss as just another draw from the same distribution.
cards.originalText: It has no risk drivers and assumes the firm’s risk exposure is unchanged over time, so it cannot show how losses respond to a changing macroeconomic environment.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: A standard loss distribution approach cannot be combined with Monte Carlo simulation, so stressed losses cannot be projected.
cards.explanation: Monte Carlo simulation of frequency and severity distributions is the core of the loss distribution approach.
cards.originalText: It cannot be combined with Monte Carlo simulation, so stressed losses cannot be projected.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: A standard loss distribution approach models only loss severity, so frequency stresses cannot be reflected.
cards.explanation: The loss distribution approach models both frequency and severity.
cards.originalText: It models only loss severity, so frequency stresses cannot be reflected.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: A standard loss distribution approach is acceptable only for regulatory capital and is prohibited by regulators for stress testing.
cards.explanation: Regulators do not prohibit the loss distribution approach for stress testing. Its real weaknesses are the lack of risk drivers and the assumption of unchanged exposure.
cards.originalText: It is acceptable only for regulatory capital and is prohibited by regulators for stress testing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: A challenge in building a conditional loss distribution approach model for stress testing is justifying the severity percentile, because the 99.9th percentile used for regulatory capital would leave the bank perpetually projected as undercapitalized.
cards.explanation: In a conditional model, frequency is forecast from macroeconomic variables and expert judgment selects the severity percentile. The capital-standard 99.9th percentile is inappropriate for stress testing.
cards.originalText: Justifying the percentile chosen for the severity distribution, because the 99.9th percentile used for regulatory capital would leave the bank perpetually projected as undercapitalized.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In operational risk stress testing, legal losses occur in the same quarter as an adverse macroeconomic shock, so the forecast must be contemporaneous with the shock.
cards.explanation: Legal losses lag macroeconomic events, sometimes by years, so the forecast must build in lags.
cards.originalText: Legal losses occur in the same quarter as an adverse macroeconomic shock, so the forecast must be contemporaneous with the shock.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Regulators require the 99.9th percentile to be used for severity in operational risk stress tests, which leaves no room for expert judgment.
cards.explanation: Regulators impose no percentile requirement for stress testing, so expert judgment is needed to choose the severity percentile.
cards.originalText: Regulators require the 99.9th percentile to be used for severity in stress tests, which leaves no room for expert judgment.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: A standard loss distribution approach is preferred over regression for operational risk stress testing because it has explicit macroeconomic risk drivers.
cards.explanation: A standard loss distribution approach has no risk drivers and is considered a secondary approach. Regression-based and conditional approaches bring in macroeconomic variables.
cards.originalText: Standard LDA is preferred over regression because it has explicit macroeconomic risk drivers.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: To forecast legal losses in an operational risk stress test, legal losses should be broken out into their own module, with lags built in between the macroeconomic drivers and the occurrence of the legal losses.
cards.explanation: Litigation losses are large, and settlements can come years after a macroeconomic shock, so the forecast must model that delay.
cards.originalText: Break legal losses out into their own module and build in lags between the macroeconomic drivers and the occurrence of the legal losses.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In an operational risk stress test, legal losses should be forecast as part of total operational losses without separating them, so that they respond immediately to the macroeconomic scenario.
cards.explanation: Legal losses should be broken out separately, and they do not respond immediately because they lag the macroeconomic event.
cards.originalText: Forecast legal losses as part of total operational losses without separating them, so they respond immediately to the macroeconomic scenario.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Legal losses should be excluded from an operational risk stress test model because they cannot be linked to the macroeconomic scenario within the stress horizon.
cards.explanation: Legal losses are material for many banks, so excluding them understates stressed losses. They should be modelled in a separate module with lags.
cards.originalText: Exclude legal losses from the model because they cannot be linked to the macroeconomic scenario within the stress horizon.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: A significant challenge in estimating the legal loss module of an operational risk stress test is that there is a lag between the macroeconomic event itself and the incurrence of legal losses.
cards.explanation: Legal losses can materialize years after the shock, so the module must include lags between its drivers and the losses.
cards.originalText: there is a lag between the macroeconomic event itself and the incurrence of legal losses.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Future litigation cases cannot be estimated in the legal loss module of an operational risk stress test.
cards.explanation: The legal loss module explicitly forecasts future litigation cases, as well as immaterial cases and losses above a threshold for current cases.
cards.originalText: future litigation cases cannot be estimated.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: Banks are minimally impacted by legal losses in operational risk stress testing.
cards.explanation: Litigation is a large share of operational losses for most banks.
cards.originalText: banks are minimally impacted by legal losses.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In operational risk stress testing, operational risks and legal losses cannot be separated.
cards.explanation: Legal losses should be broken out as a separate module of the stress test.
cards.originalText: operational risks and legal losses cannot be separated.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In a comprehensive operational risk stress testing framework, risks that apply only to each unique bank are best captured in the idiosyncratic scenario add-on module.
cards.explanation: The framework has three modules: the expected nonlegal loss forecast, the legal loss module and the idiosyncratic scenario add-on. Bank-specific vulnerabilities and storylines belong in the add-on.
cards.originalText: Idiosyncratic scenario add‑on.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In a comprehensive operational risk stress testing framework, the legal loss module is the one that best captures risks applicable only to each unique bank.
cards.explanation: The legal loss module covers litigation losses only. Bank-specific risks are captured by the idiosyncratic scenario add-on.
cards.originalText: Legal loss.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.loText: Explain challenges and considerations when developing and implementing models used in stress testing operational risk.
cards.reading: ORR-7: Integrated Risk Management
cards.statement: In a comprehensive operational risk stress testing framework, the expected nonlegal loss forecast module is the one that best captures risks applicable only to each unique bank.
cards.explanation: The expected nonlegal loss forecast projects losses by risk type from quantitative models refined by expert judgment. Bank-specific storylines belong in the idiosyncratic scenario add-on.
cards.originalText: Expected nonlegal loss forecast.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: In the Basel Committee's 2018 report on cyber-resilience practices, Singapore's guidance focuses on the early detection of cyber intrusions.
cards.explanation: Each jurisdiction's guidance has a different emphasis. Singapore stresses early detection of intrusions.
cards.originalText: Singapore: early detection of cyber intrusions

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: In the Basel Committee's 2018 report on cyber-resilience practices, Hong Kong's guidance focuses on common procedures and methodologies for the assessment of ICT risk.
cards.explanation: Hong Kong's guidance concerns the importance of effective cyber-security risk management. Common procedures and methodologies for assessing ICT risk are the focus of the European Banking Authority.
cards.originalText: Hong Kong: common procedures and methodologies for the assessment of ICT risk
cards.correction: In the Basel Committee's 2018 report on cyber-resilience practices, Hong Kong's guidance focuses on the importance of effective cyber-security risk management.

changes.from: common procedures and methodologies for the assessment of ICT risk
changes.to: the importance of effective cyber-security risk management

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: In the Basel Committee's 2018 report on cyber-resilience practices, Brazil's guidance focuses on the importance of effective cyber-security risk management.
cards.explanation: Brazil's guidance concerns the establishment of a cyber security policy. The importance of effective cyber-security risk management is Hong Kong's focus.
cards.originalText: Brazil: the importance of effective cyber‑security risk management
cards.correction: In the Basel Committee's 2018 report on cyber-resilience practices, Brazil's guidance focuses on the establishment of a cyber security policy.

changes.from: the importance of effective cyber-security risk management
changes.to: the establishment of a cyber security policy

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: In the Basel Committee's 2018 report on cyber-resilience practices, the European Banking Authority's guidance focuses on the establishment of a cyber security policy.
cards.explanation: The EBA's guidance concerns common procedures and methodologies for assessing ICT risk. Establishing a cyber security policy is Brazil's focus.
cards.originalText: European Banking Authority: the establishment of a cyber security policy
cards.correction: In the Basel Committee's 2018 report on cyber-resilience practices, the European Banking Authority's guidance focuses on common procedures and methodologies for the assessment of ICT risk.

changes.from: the establishment of a cyber security policy
changes.to: common procedures and methodologies for the assessment of ICT risk

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: The FSB Lexicon definition of cyber-resilience means eliminating all cyber vulnerabilities so that incidents cannot occur.
cards.explanation: Cyber-resilience is the ability to continue to carry out the organisation's mission by anticipating and adapting to threats and by withstanding, containing and rapidly recovering from incidents. It accepts that incidents will occur.
cards.originalText: Eliminating all cyber vulnerabilities so that incidents cannot occur

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Under the FSB Lexicon definition, cyber-resilience includes anticipating and adapting to cyber threats and other relevant changes in the environment.
cards.explanation: Anticipating and adapting is one element of the definition, alongside withstanding, containing and rapidly recovering from incidents.
cards.originalText: Anticipating and adapting to cyber threats and other relevant changes in the environment

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Under the FSB Lexicon definition, cyber-resilience includes withstanding, containing and rapidly recovering from cyber incidents.
cards.explanation: This is the second element of the definition, alongside anticipating and adapting to threats.
cards.originalText: Withstanding, containing and rapidly recovering from cyber incidents

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Under the FSB Lexicon definition, cyber-resilience is the ability of an organisation to continue to carry out its mission.
cards.explanation: Continuing the mission is the core of the definition.
cards.originalText: Continuing to carry out the organisation’s mission

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: According to the Basel Committee, greater use of automation, third-party service providers and cloud services grows the attack surface, enlarges the perimeter of interest to regulators, and with cloud services makes that perimeter shared.
cards.explanation: More automation and integration produce an attack surface accessible from anywhere. Third-party use enlarges the regulatory perimeter, and a shared perimeter means institutions must build resilience in partnership with providers.
cards.originalText: The attack surface grows and is accessible from anywhere, the perimeter of interest to regulators becomes bigger with third‑party use, and cloud services make that perimeter shared

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: According to the Basel Committee, outsourcing data processing to third parties shrinks the regulators' perimeter of interest because the data are held outside the institution.
cards.explanation: Third-party use enlarges, not shrinks, the perimeter of interest to regulators.
cards.originalText: Outsourcing data processing to third parties shrinks the regulators’ perimeter of interest because data is held outside the institution

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: According to the Basel Committee, cloud services make the perimeter the sole responsibility of the cloud provider, so the bank's own cyber-resilience duties fall away.
cards.explanation: The perimeter becomes shared, not transferred. The institution must still build and maintain its own cyber-resilience in partnership with the provider.
cards.originalText: Cloud services make the perimeter the sole responsibility of the cloud provider, so the bank’s own cyber‑resilience duties fall away

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Define cyber-resilience and compare recent regulatory initiatives in the area of cyber-resilience.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: According to the Basel Committee, greater automation reduces the attack surface, which lowers the incentive for cyber-adversaries to increase their capabilities.
cards.explanation: Greater automation and integration enlarge the attack surface, which gives adversaries more incentive to increase their capabilities.
cards.originalText: Greater automation reduces the attack surface, which lowers the incentive for cyber‑adversaries to increase their capabilities

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain and assess current practices for the sharing of cybersecurity information between different types of institutions.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Sharing of cybersecurity information among regulators is the least commonly observed type of information sharing across jurisdictions.
cards.explanation: Sharing among regulators is typically ad hoc, bilateral or within supervisory colleges, with less systematic arrangements.
cards.originalText: Sharing among regulators

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain and assess current practices for the sharing of cybersecurity information between different types of institutions.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Sharing of cybersecurity information among banks is the least commonly observed type of information sharing across jurisdictions.
cards.explanation: Sharing among banks is one of the three most commonly observed types, together with sharing by banks and regulators with security agencies and sharing from banks to regulators.
cards.originalText: Sharing among banks

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain and assess current practices for the sharing of cybersecurity information between different types of institutions.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Sharing of cybersecurity information by banks and regulators with security agencies is the least commonly observed type of information sharing across jurisdictions.
cards.explanation: Sharing with security agencies is one of the three most commonly observed types. Sharing among regulators is the least observed.
cards.originalText: Sharing by banks and regulators with security agencies

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain and assess current practices for the sharing of cybersecurity information between different types of institutions.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: The scope and depth of cybersecurity information sharing among banks may vary significantly between financial markets, depending on the level of trust among participating banks.
cards.explanation: Sharing among banks relies on trust and industry culture, so it often starts within a small group before widening.
cards.originalText: The scope and depth of information‑sharing practices among banks may significantly vary between financial markets, depending on the level of trust among participating banks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain and assess current practices for the sharing of cybersecurity information between different types of institutions.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Sharing of cybersecurity information among banks is less frequently observed and generally considered less effective than other cybersecurity information-sharing practices.
cards.explanation: Sharing among banks is one of the three most commonly observed types of cybersecurity information sharing.
cards.originalText: The sharing of cybersecurity information among banks is less frequently observed and generally considered to be less effective than other cyber‑security information‑sharing practices.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain and assess current practices for the sharing of cybersecurity information between different types of institutions.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Information sharing among different national regulators has evolved significantly over the past several years and is now a widespread practice in a large majority of jurisdictions.
cards.explanation: Sharing among regulators is the least observed type and remains largely ad hoc.
cards.originalText: Information‑sharing among different national regulators has evolved significantly over the past several years and is now a widespread practice at a large majority of jurisdictions.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain and assess current practices for the sharing of cybersecurity information between different types of institutions.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: Existing peer-sharing mechanisms among banks focus on exchanging information on cyber-security incidents, but such information is generally not shared from banks to regulators.
cards.explanation: Banks do share incident information with regulators, frequently because it is mandated. Peer sharing mainly concerns threat information.
cards.originalText: Existing peer‑sharing mechanisms among banks focus on the exchange of information related to cyber‑security incidents, but such information is generally not shared from banks to regulators.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.loText: Explain and assess current practices for the sharing of cybersecurity information between different types of institutions.
cards.reading: ORR-8: Cyber-resilience: Range of Practices
cards.statement: In jurisdictions where information sharing among banks is already well established, sharing of cybersecurity information from banks to regulators tends to be less prevalent.
cards.explanation: Bank-to-regulator reporting is usually mandated and is not displaced by peer sharing among banks.
cards.originalText: Sharing from banks to regulators

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: A stress test modeler must consider capital actions such as acquisitions, spin-offs, dividend changes and share repurchases or issuance, because they deplete or conserve capital.
cards.explanation: Each quarter the modeler must make assumptions about these actions, which makes projecting the balance sheet over the horizon difficult.
cards.originalText: Greta and Dace only.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Balance sheet modeling for a stress test is difficult only if a dynamic balance sheet is assumed; under a static balance sheet the modeler need not consider capital actions.
cards.explanation: The difficulty of modeling the balance sheet and capital actions exists under both static and dynamic balance sheet assumptions.
cards.originalText: John only.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Regardless of whether the denominator of the capital ratio is common equity or risk-weighted assets, determining post-stress capital adequacy requires modeling both the income statement and the balance sheet over the stress test horizon, which is typically about two years.
cards.explanation: Post-stress capital ratios depend on the evolution of both flows (income) and stocks (balance sheet) over the horizon.
cards.originalText: Regardless of whether the denominator in the capital ratio is common equity or risk‑weighted assets (RWA), determining post‑stress capital adequacy requires modeling both the income statement and the balance sheet over the course of the stress test horizon, which is typically about two years

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Compared to the banking book, stress testing the trading book is more difficult because it is a newer discipline.
cards.explanation: Formal stress testing of the banking book, dominated by credit risk, is the newer discipline, and implementing stress scenarios in the trading book is more straightforward.
cards.originalText: Compared to the banking book, stress testing the trading book is more difficult because it is a newer discipline

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Implementing stress scenarios for revenues is much more developed and easier than stress testing for losses.
cards.explanation: Revenue modeling is far less developed and harder than loss modeling.
cards.originalText: Implementing stress scenarios for revenues is much more developed and easier than stress testing for losses

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: The most robust stress tests assume loss severity rates (loss given default) that are invariant to geography, business cycle or industry and uniformly represent worst-case scenarios.
cards.explanation: Loss given default varies with geography, the business cycle and industry. One-size-fits-all severities make the mapping from macro factors to bank results less meaningful.
cards.originalText: The most robust stress tests assume loss severity (i.e., loss given default, LGD) rates that are invariant to geography, business cycle, or industry and uniformly represent the worst‑case scenarios

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Credit card loan losses are especially sensitive to unemployment rates, so regional differences in unemployment produce very different card loss rates.
cards.explanation: This is why macro-variable stress tests can mislead for banks exposed to different geographies, as shown by the wide range of US state unemployment rates after the 2007-2009 crisis.
cards.originalText: Credit card loans.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Assumptions about acquisitions and spin-offs, dividend changes, and share buybacks or issuance make it especially challenging to model a bank's balance sheet over a stress test horizon.
cards.explanation: These capital actions change both capital and assets each quarter, so the balance sheet path requires many judgment-based assumptions.
cards.originalText: model a bank’s balance sheet over a stress test horizon.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: In modeling bank revenues over a stress test horizon, total income is split into interest and noninterest income, and noninterest income (fees, service charges) is especially hard to model even though its share of bank income has been rising.
cards.explanation: Noninterest income is increasingly important but the hardest part of revenue to model.
cards.originalText: Total income is split into interest and noninterest income; noninterest income (fees, service charges) is especially hard to model, even though its share of bank income has been rising.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Revenue modeling is more developed than loss modeling because the 2009 SCAP specified a detailed revenue methodology.
cards.explanation: The SCAP gave little guidance on revenue, and revenue modeling remains much less developed than loss modeling.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Interest income is easy to model for stress testing because the yield curve fully determines how changing rates affect bank profitability.
cards.explanation: The yield curve helps estimate interest income, but how rate changes affect overall profitability remains unclear.
cards.originalText: Interest income is easy to model because the yield curve fully determines how changing rates affect bank profitability.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling a bank’s revenues, losses, and its balance sheet over a stress test horizon period.
cards.reading: ORR-17: Stress Testing Banks
cards.statement: Noninterest income can be ignored in stress testing because it is a small and declining share of US bank income.
cards.explanation: The share of noninterest income in bank income has been steadily increasing, so ignoring it would be a serious omission.
cards.originalText: Noninterest income can be ignored because it is a small and declining share of U.S. bank income.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In the RAROC measure, the numerator is after-tax expected risk-adjusted net income and the denominator is economic capital.
cards.explanation: RAROC divides after-tax expected income, net of expected losses, by economic capital, which proxies for risk.
cards.originalText: The numerator is after‑tax expected risk‑adjusted net income and the denominator is economic capital.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: The numerator of RAROC is pretax risk-adjusted net income.
cards.explanation: Taxes are deducted in the numerator, so RAROC uses after-tax expected risk-adjusted net income.
cards.originalText: The numerator is pretax risk‑adjusted net income.
cards.correction: The numerator of RAROC is after-tax risk-adjusted net income.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Regulatory capital is the denominator of RAROC.
cards.explanation: The denominator of RAROC is economic capital, a proxy for risk, rather than the rule-based regulatory capital amount.
cards.originalText: Regulatory capital is the denominator.
cards.correction: Economic capital is the denominator of RAROC.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In the RAROC numerator, expected losses are set to zero when the activity is a credit exposure.
cards.explanation: For credit exposures, expected default losses are the main expected loss deducted from the numerator.
cards.originalText: Expected losses are set to zero in the numerator when the activity is a credit exposure.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In the RAROC formula, the denominator is economic capital, the buffer held against unexpected losses at the bank's chosen confidence level, which serves as the proxy for risk.
cards.explanation: The numerator measures reward and the denominator measures risk, which captures the risk-reward trade-off.
cards.originalText: Economic capital, the buffer held against unexpected losses at the bank’s chosen confidence level, which serves as the proxy for risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In the RAROC formula, the denominator is the loan amount, which proxies for the revenue the loan can generate.
cards.explanation: The denominator is economic capital, which measures risk. The loan amount is not the denominator.
cards.originalText: The loan amount, which proxies for the revenue the loan can generate.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In the RAROC formula, the denominator is the bank's cost of capital, used as the benchmark that the loan's return must exceed.
cards.explanation: The cost of equity or hurdle rate is the benchmark that RAROC is compared with. It is not the denominator.
cards.originalText: The bank’s cost of capital, used as the benchmark that the loan’s return must exceed.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Net present value is incompatible with the CAPM and has no convenient way of incorporating risk.
cards.explanation: NPV is built on the CAPM and incorporates risk through a risk-adjusted discount rate based on beta.
cards.originalText: NPV is incompatible with the CAPM and has no convenient way of incorporating risk.
cards.correction: Net present value uses a CAPM-based risk-adjusted discount rate to incorporate risk.

changes.from: is incompatible with the CAPM and has no convenient way of incorporating risk
changes.to: uses a CAPM-based risk-adjusted discount rate to incorporate risk

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: RAROC adjusts the numerator by deducting expected loss from the return and adjusts the denominator by substituting economic capital for accounting capital.
cards.explanation: These are the two adjustments that turn a simple return on capital measure into RAROC.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Return on equity and return on assets rely on accounting book values and therefore do not capture the underlying risk.
cards.explanation: Accounting measures ignore risk, which is the gap that RAROC is designed to fill.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: RAROC can be used for capital allocation on an ex ante basis, using expected revenues and losses, and for performance evaluation on an ex post basis, using realized revenues and losses.
cards.explanation: Ex ante, RAROC guides capital allocation with expected figures. Ex post, it judges performance against realized outcomes.
cards.originalText: All four

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: If a business unit's cost of equity is greater than its RAROC, the business unit is not adding value for shareholders.
cards.explanation: The cost of equity is the minimum return shareholders require, so a RAROC below it means value destruction.
cards.originalText: If a business unit’s cost of equity is greater than its RAROC, then the business unit is not adding value to shareholders.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In the context of performance measurement, RAROC uses accounting profits.
cards.explanation: RAROC is based on economic profits, with expected losses deducted and economic capital in the denominator.
cards.correction: In the context of performance measurement, RAROC uses economic profits.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In the numerator of the RAROC equation, expected loss is added to the return.
cards.explanation: Expected loss is deducted from the return in the numerator.
cards.correction: In the numerator of the RAROC equation, expected loss is deducted from the return.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: RAROC is useful for determining incentive compensation, but it lacks the flexibility to consider deferred or contingent compensation.
cards.explanation: RAROC is flexible enough to accommodate deferred or contingent compensation and clawbacks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges that arise when using RAROC for performance measurement, including choosing a time horizon, measuring default probability, and choosing a confidence level.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Choosing a lower confidence level is not likely to reduce the amount of risk capital required if the firm has little exposure to operational, credit and settlement risks.
cards.explanation: A lower confidence level cuts risk capital sharply mainly for firms dominated by risks with rare, very large losses, such as operational, credit and settlement risks.
cards.originalText: II only.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges that arise when using RAROC for performance measurement, including choosing a time horizon, measuring default probability, and choosing a confidence level.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Selecting a longer time horizon for RAROC calculations is preferable because risk and return data are more reliable with more time.
cards.explanation: Practitioners use a one-year horizon, reflecting the business planning cycle and time to recapitalize. Risk and return data beyond one year are of low quality.
cards.originalText: I only.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges that arise when using RAROC for performance measurement, including choosing a time horizon, measuring default probability, and choosing a confidence level.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: A through-the-cycle (TTC) approach to default probabilities is more likely to result in lower volatility of capital than a point-in-time (PIT) approach.
cards.explanation: TTC probabilities smooth the economic cycle, so ratings and economic capital are more stable than under PIT.
cards.originalText: A TTC approach is more likely to result in a lower volatility of capital compared to the PIT approach.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges that arise when using RAROC for performance measurement, including choosing a time horizon, measuring default probability, and choosing a confidence level.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: A through-the-cycle (TTC) approach should be used to price financial instruments with credit risk exposure.
cards.explanation: Pricing credit-risk instruments uses the point-in-time approach, which reflects current conditions.
cards.originalText: A through‑the‑cycle (TTC) approach should be used to price financial instruments with credit risk exposure.
cards.correction: A point-in-time (PIT) approach should be used to price financial instruments with credit risk exposure.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges that arise when using RAROC for performance measurement, including choosing a time horizon, measuring default probability, and choosing a confidence level.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: A point-in-time (PIT) approach is more commonly used for computations involving profitability and strategic decisions.
cards.explanation: The through-the-cycle approach is more commonly used for economic capital, profitability and strategic decisions.
cards.originalText: A point‑in‑time (PIT) approach is more commonly used for computations involving profitability and strategic decisions.
cards.correction: A through-the-cycle (TTC) approach is more commonly used for computations involving profitability and strategic decisions.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges that arise when using RAROC for performance measurement, including choosing a time horizon, measuring default probability, and choosing a confidence level.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: A firm's rating will not change when analyzed under the point-in-time approach versus the through-the-cycle approach.
cards.explanation: Ratings are more likely to change under PIT than under TTC, because PIT responds to current conditions.
cards.originalText: A firm’s rating will not change when analyzed under the PIT approach versus the TTC approach.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling diversification benefits, including aggregating a firm’s risk capital and allocating economic capital to different business lines.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Large diversification benefits can arise when operational risk is aggregated with other risks.
cards.explanation: Operational risk is relatively weakly correlated with market and credit risk, so the aggregate capital is well below the simple sum.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling diversification benefits, including aggregating a firm’s risk capital and allocating economic capital to different business lines.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Diversification can be achieved only across different risk classes, never within one risk class.
cards.explanation: Diversification benefits also arise across business lines and activities within a single risk type.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling diversification benefits, including aggregating a firm’s risk capital and allocating economic capital to different business lines.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: The diversification benefit of the firm can be allocated back to business units in an objective way, with no subjectivity.
cards.explanation: Allocating the diversification benefit to units is highly subjective and affects their performance measures.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling diversification benefits, including aggregating a firm’s risk capital and allocating economic capital to different business lines.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: A diversification benefit exists whenever the correlation between two risks is exactly +1.
cards.explanation: At a correlation of +1 the aggregate equals the simple sum, so there is no diversification benefit.
cards.correction: A diversification benefit exists whenever the correlation between two risks is below +1.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling diversification benefits, including aggregating a firm’s risk capital and allocating economic capital to different business lines.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Fully diversified capital should be used to assess the firm's solvency and minimum risk pricing.
cards.explanation: Fully diversified capital allocates the whole diversification benefit, so the allocations add up to the firm's total risk capital.
cards.originalText: Fully diversified capital (\$56 for X and \$64 for Y) should be used to assess the firm’s solvency and minimum risk pricing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling diversification benefits, including aggregating a firm’s risk capital and allocating economic capital to different business lines.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Incremental (marginal) capital should be used for active portfolio management and business mix decisions.
cards.explanation: Marginal capital fully reflects diversification effects, so it suits decisions on adding or removing activities.
cards.originalText: Incremental capital (\$40 for X and \$50 for Y) should be used for active portfolio management and business mix decisions.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain challenges in modeling diversification benefits, including aggregating a firm’s risk capital and allocating economic capital to different business lines.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Stand-alone capital can be used for incentive compensation, while fully diversified capital can be used to assess the extra performance generated by diversification.
cards.explanation: These are the standard uses of the stand-alone and fully diversified capital measures.
cards.originalText: Stand‑alone capital can be used for incentive compensation, while fully diversified capital can be used to assess the extra performance generated by diversification.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: When business units complain that a RAROC system attributes too much economic capital to them, senior management should display commitment to RAROC and expand in-house communication and education about the system.
cards.explanation: Best practice pairs visible top-management commitment with transparent communication and education so that capital allocation is seen as fair.
cards.originalText: Display commitment to RAROC, expand in‑house communication and education regarding the system.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: When business units are dissatisfied with a RAROC system, senior management should neglect the dissatisfaction and enforce the system at all costs.
cards.explanation: Ignoring concerns breeds resistance. Best practice calls for open dialogue, communication and education.
cards.originalText: Neglect dissatisfaction in the local management and enforce the RAROC system at all costs.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Implementing a RAROC system tends to decrease the frequency of risk parameter reviews.
cards.explanation: Economic capital depends on risk parameters such as PD, LGD, volatility and correlation, so these must be reviewed more, not less, frequently.
cards.originalText: Decrease in the frequency of risk parameter reviews
cards.correction: Implementing a RAROC system tends to increase the frequency of risk parameter reviews.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Implementing a RAROC system tends to increase disputes over economic capital allocations.
cards.explanation: Explicit economic capital charges make business units challenge the fairness of their allocations.
cards.originalText: Increase in disputes over economic capital allocations

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
