cards.statement: Implementing a RAROC system tends to cause resources to be reallocated from lower-RAROC units to higher-RAROC units.
cards.explanation: RAROC works like an internal capital market that directs scarce resources toward higher-RAROC units.
cards.originalText: Reallocation of resources from lower to higher RAROC units

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Implementing a RAROC system tends to increase activity in the parameter review group.
cards.explanation: Because economic capital is sensitive to the parameters, the review group becomes more important.
cards.originalText: Increased activity in the parameter review group

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Best practice in implementing RAROC calls for an exclusively quantitative decision rule under which the firm exits any activity whose ex-ante RAROC does not exceed the hurdle rate.
cards.explanation: Best practice combines RAROC, the quantity of earnings, with qualitative quality-of-earnings factors. An exclusively quantitative exit rule ignores strategic value.
cards.originalText: In order to preserve the integrity and transparency of the RAROC system, there should be an exclusively quantitative decision rule for activities: if the ex‑ante RAROC does not exceed the firm’s hurdle rate (if the RAROC return is ”low”), the firm should exit the activity

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In implementing a RAROC system, the instructions must come from top management, and the CEO and executive team should sponsor the implementation and be active in its diffusion.
cards.explanation: RAROC steers strategic decisions, so senior management commitment is the first recommendation for implementation.
cards.originalText: Given the strategic nature of the decisions steered by a RAROC system, the marching orders must come from the top management of the firm; specifically, the CEO and his or her executive team should sponsor the implementation of a RAROC system and should be active in its diffusion

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: The value at risk methodologies for measuring market risk and credit risk that underpin RAROC calculations are generally well accepted by business units, although this is not yet true for operational risk; disagreements in practice concern the parameters that determine the size of economic capital.
cards.explanation: Market and credit risk methods are comparatively accepted, while operational risk measurement is less established.
cards.originalText: The value at risk (VaR) methodologies for measuring market risk and credit risk that underpin RAROC calculations are ”generally well‑accepted” by business units (although this is not yet true for operational risk); in practice, disagreements concern the setting of the parameters that feed into these models which determine the size of economic capital

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Balance sheet requests from business units, such as economic capital, leverage ratio, liquidity ratios and risk-weighted assets, should be channeled to the RAROC group every quarter, after which limits are set for these measures.
cards.explanation: This quarterly process is part of active capital management within a RAROC system.
cards.originalText: Balance sheet requests from the business units, such as economic capital, leverage ratio, liquidity ratios, and risk‑weighted assets, should be channeled to the RAROC group every quarter; limits are then set for economic capital, leverage ratio, liquidity ratios, and risk‑weighted assets

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: A restriction on the firm's growth due to leverage limitations may result in higher profits.
cards.explanation: Leverage limits force the firm to allocate scarce capital to its best risk-adjusted uses, which can raise profitability.
cards.originalText: A restriction on the firm’s growth due to leverage limitations may result in higher profits.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: A successful RAROC approach focuses on maximizing the profits earned by the firm.
cards.explanation: RAROC focuses on how well the firm is compensated for the risks taken, not on the amount of income generated.
cards.originalText: A successful RAROC approach is focused on maximizing profits earned by the firm.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: In a RAROC approach, data collection throughout the firm should be decentralized so that business units can ensure the utmost accuracy of data.
cards.explanation: Data collection should be centralized with edit and reasonability checks. The RAROC group is accountable for it, and units are accountable only for the data they produce.
cards.originalText: The data collection process throughout the firm should be decentralized to allow the various business units to ensure the utmost accuracy of data.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.loText: Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
cards.reading: ORR-18: Risk Capital Attribution and Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement
cards.statement: Metrics involving credit risk, market risk and operational risk used to compute economic capital are generally clearly defined and may be computed objectively.
cards.explanation: Credit and market risk metrics are comparatively well defined, but operational risk metrics involve significant subjectivity and debate.
cards.originalText: Metrics involving credit risk, market risk, and operational risk to compute economic capital are generally clearly defined and may be computed objectively.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.loText: Within the economic capital implementation framework, describe the challenges that appear in: - Defining and calculating risk measures - Risk aggregation - Validation of models - Dependency modeling in credit risk - Evaluating counterparty credit risk - Assessing interest rate risk in the banking book
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: All major copulas automatically ensure that Pearson linear correlation accurately describes the true dependence structure, even when dependence is dynamic.
cards.explanation: Linear correlation is not the only dependence measure, and a copula does not guarantee a correct or time-varying dependence structure. Its parameters still have to be estimated and validated.
cards.originalText: Pearson linear correlation is the only dependence input available, but all major copulas automatically ensure it accurately describes the true dependence structure even when dependence is dynamic.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.loText: Within the economic capital implementation framework, describe the challenges that appear in: - Defining and calculating risk measures - Risk aggregation - Validation of models - Dependency modeling in credit risk - Evaluating counterparty credit risk - Assessing interest rate risk in the banking book
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: The copula approach allows simulation of the entire distribution of aggregate losses, not only the tails.
cards.explanation: Simulating from the copula gives the whole aggregate loss distribution.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.loText: Within the economic capital implementation framework, describe the challenges that appear in: - Defining and calculating risk measures - Risk aggregation - Validation of models - Dependency modeling in credit risk - Evaluating counterparty credit risk - Assessing interest rate risk in the banking book
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: Given the same marginal distributions, different copula functions can be simulated to see the effect of the assumed dependence structure.
cards.explanation: A copula separates the marginal distributions from the dependence structure, so copulas such as the Gaussian and t can be swapped as a sensitivity test.
cards.originalText: Given the same marginal distributions, she can test (simulate) different copula functions to see the effect of the assumed dependence structure.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.loText: Within the economic capital implementation framework, describe the challenges that appear in: - Defining and calculating risk measures - Risk aggregation - Validation of models - Dependency modeling in credit risk - Evaluating counterparty credit risk - Assessing interest rate risk in the banking book
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: A copula places no requirement on the form of the marginal distributions it joins, so the marginals may be skewed or heavy-tailed.
cards.explanation: Because the dependence structure is modeled separately, the marginals can take any form.
cards.originalText: The marginals may be skewed or heavy‑tailed, because a copula places no requirement on the form of the univariate distributions it joins.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.loText: Within the economic capital implementation framework, describe the challenges that appear in: - Defining and calculating risk measures - Risk aggregation - Validation of models - Dependency modeling in credit risk - Evaluating counterparty credit risk - Assessing interest rate risk in the banking book
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks

cards.statement: Bonds with embedded options pose a greater challenge to the determination of a bank's economic capital than ordinary stocks, preference shares or plain fixed-rate loans, because embedded optionality makes cash flows uncertain and payoffs nonlinear.
cards.explanation: Exercise of the options depends on borrower behavior and future rates, so a simple linear sensitivity measure understates the risk.

cards.statement: Capturing wrong-way risk in economic capital for counterparty credit risk is difficult because it requires understanding the counterparty's often opaque market risk factor sensitivities and comparing them with the bank's own exposures, and because its magnitude is hard to quantify over a one-year horizon at a high confidence level.
cards.explanation: Wrong-way risk arises when exposure to a counterparty rises at the same time as its credit quality deteriorates.
cards.originalText: Identifying it requires understanding the counterparty’s market risk factor sensitivities (often opaque, e.g., a hedge fund) and comparing them with the bank’s own exposures, and its magnitude is hard to quantify over a one‑year horizon at a high confidence level.

cards.statement: The main challenge in choosing a risk measure for economic capital purposes is that there is no singularly preferred risk measure.
cards.explanation: Standard deviation, VaR, expected shortfall and spectral measures each have advantages and disadvantages, so the choice must fit the intended application.
cards.originalText: There is no singularly preferred risk measure for economic capital purposes.

cards.statement: The main challenge in choosing a risk measure for economic capital purposes is that there are no generally accepted properties of a good risk measure.
cards.explanation: There is general agreement on desirable properties, such as being intuitive, stable, easy to compute and coherent. The difficulty is that no measure satisfies all of them.
cards.originalText: There are no generally accepted properties of a good risk measure.

cards.statement: Combining economic capital components that were calculated at different confidence levels and time horizons, without first expressing them on a common basis, makes the aggregate figure inaccurate.
cards.explanation: Aggregation requires comparable units, meaning the same risk metric, confidence level and time horizon.
cards.originalText: Combining component measures that were calculated at different confidence levels and time horizons without first expressing them on a common basis.

cards.statement: Counterparty credit exposure cannot be netted across counterparties, so it must be calculated at the netting-set level for thousands of counterparties and over many future holding periods, which greatly increases computational intensity.
cards.explanation: Unlike market risk VaR, where gains on one position offset losses on another, exposure cannot be netted across counterparties. Each netting set must be simulated over many future holding periods, so the computation is very intensive.
cards.originalText: Exposure cannot be netted across counterparties, so it must be calculated at the netting‑set level for thousands of counterparties and over many future holding periods, greatly increasing computational intensity.

cards.statement: Counterparty credit exposure is measured over a single short holding period.
cards.explanation: Market risk VaR uses a short holding period, but counterparty exposure must be simulated over multiple, long future holding periods (years or even decades).
cards.originalText: Counterparty exposure is measured over a single short holding period, which is too short for derivatives.
cards.correction: Counterparty credit exposure is measured over multiple long future holding periods.

cards.statement: The long holding period of balance sheet assets and liabilities is one of the main challenges in calculating economic capital for interest rate risk in the banking book.
cards.explanation: Banking-book positions are held for a long time and their cash flows are uncertain because of embedded optionality such as prepayment and non-maturity deposits. Together these make the capital computation difficult.
cards.originalText: The long holding period of balance sheet assets and liabilities.

cards.statement: Copulas are more flexible than a covariance matrix and allow for nonlinearities and higher-order dependencies.
cards.explanation: A copula joins the marginal distributions into a joint distribution with flexible functional forms, so it relaxes the linear-correlation limitation of the covariance matrix. Its drawbacks are that the parameterization is hard to validate and the joint distribution is hard to build.
cards.originalText: Is more flexible than a covariance matrix and allows for nonlinearities and higher‑order dependencies.

cards.statement: With fixed (constant) diversification, the diversification effect is sensitive to the underlying interactions between the different risk components.
cards.explanation: Constant diversification simply subtracts a fixed percentage from the sum of the risks, so it is insensitive to the underlying interactions between risk types.
cards.originalText: The effect of fixed diversification is sensitive to underlying interactions between the different components.
cards.correction: With fixed (constant) diversification, the diversification effect is insensitive to the underlying interactions between the different risk components.

cards.statement: The variance-covariance matrix approach to risk aggregation makes inter-risk correlations easy to estimate.
cards.explanation: Under the variance-covariance approach the correlations between risk types are difficult to estimate, and the linear structure also misses nonlinearities in the dependence.
cards.originalText: The method is easy to use as it easily estimates inter‑risk correlations and does not capture nonlinearities.
cards.correction: The variance-covariance matrix approach to risk aggregation makes inter-risk correlations difficult to estimate.

cards.statement: Complex simulation is one of the characteristics of the unit of account used in risk aggregation.
cards.explanation: The unit of account is defined by three characteristics: the risk metric, the confidence level and the time horizon. Simulation is a method for combining risks, not a characteristic of the common risk currency.

cards.statement: The risk metric is one of the characteristics of the unit of account used in risk aggregation.
cards.explanation: The unit of account puts different risk types into comparable units and is defined by the risk metric, the confidence level and the time horizon.

cards.statement: The time horizon is one of the characteristics of the unit of account used in risk aggregation.

cards.statement: Precision is one of the desirable characteristics of a risk measure listed by the BIS for use in an economic capital framework.
cards.explanation: The BIS list covers qualities such as being intuitive, stable, easy to compute, easy to understand, coherent and interpretable in economic terms. Precision is not on the list, because no measure is perfect and estimates depend on model assumptions.

cards.statement: Coherence is a desirable characteristic of a risk measure within the economic capital framework.
cards.explanation: A coherent risk measure satisfies monotonicity, positive homogeneity, translation invariance and subadditivity, and coherence is one of the characteristics the BIS lists as desirable.

cards.statement: Being easy to compute is a desirable characteristic of a risk measure within the economic capital framework.

cards.statement: Standard deviation is not a coherent risk measure because it violates the monotonicity condition.
cards.explanation: Standard deviation treats upside and downside dispersion alike, so it can rank a portfolio that always pays at least as much as another as the riskier one. This violates monotonicity, and it is also not stable.

cards.statement: Earnings at risk (EaR) is a main source of interest rate risk in the banking book.
cards.explanation: The main sources are repricing risk, yield curve risk and basis risk. Earnings at risk is a measurement approach that quantifies the loss of net interest income from rate changes, not a source of risk.

cards.statement: Repricing risk is a main source of interest rate risk in the banking book.
cards.explanation: Repricing risk arises from differences in the maturity or repricing terms of assets and liabilities. The other main sources are yield curve risk and basis risk.
cards.originalText: Repricing risk

cards.statement: Basis risk is a main source of interest rate risk in the banking book.
cards.explanation: Basis risk arises from the imperfect correlation between the rates earned and paid on instruments with similar repricing characteristics.
cards.originalText: Basis risk

cards.statement: The most conservative estimate of risk is always a simple aggregation of compartmentalized measures.
cards.explanation: Summing separately measured risks is usually conservative, but interactions between risk types can compound so that true integrated risk exceeds the simple sum. For example, FX moves can raise default probabilities on foreign-currency loans.
cards.originalText: The most conservative estimate of risk is always a simple aggregation of compartmentalized measures
cards.correction: The most conservative estimate of risk is not always a simple aggregation of compartmentalized measures.

cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: A compartmentalized approach sums risks measured separately, while a unified approach considers the interaction between these risks explicitly.
cards.explanation: This is the basic contrast the Basel Committee draws between the two approaches to risk measurement.
cards.originalText: A compartmentalized approach sums risks measured separately, while a unified approach considers the interaction between these risks explicitly

cards.statement: From a theoretical perspective, an integrated approach is needed to capture potential compounding effects that are ignored in compartmentalized risk measurement approaches.
cards.explanation: Only an approach that models the interaction between risk types can capture compounding effects, such as foreign-currency loans whose default risk rises when the exchange rate moves against the borrower.
cards.originalText: From a theoretical perspective, an integrated approach is needed to capture potential compounding effects that are ignored in compartmentalized risk measurement approaches

cards.statement: VaR is not subadditive, so the sum of sub-portfolio VaRs can understate the bank-wide VaR.
cards.explanation: Because VaR can violate subadditivity, the bank-wide VaR of a combined portfolio can exceed the sum of the stand-alone VaRs. This causes problems when VaR is used to allocate economic capital and set limits.
cards.originalText: VaR is not subadditive, so the sum of sub‑portfolio VaRs can understate the bank‑wide VaR

cards.statement: VaR violates the monotonicity condition, so a portfolio with higher future returns can show greater risk.
cards.explanation: VaR is monotonic. The monotonicity violation is the criticism of standard deviation, while the main coherence criticism of VaR is that it can violate subadditivity.
cards.originalText: VaR violates monotonicity, so a portfolio with higher future returns can show greater risk

cards.statement: VaR has no clear link to the bank's desired target credit rating.
cards.explanation: VaR is a quantile at a chosen confidence level, which maps directly to a target default probability and hence to a target rating. The lack of a clear link to the target rating is the criticism of expected shortfall.

cards.statement: Retail non-maturity deposits are appropriately modeled as floating-rate, putable bonds.
cards.explanation: The bank can reset the deposit rate, which makes the deposit behave like a floating-rate bond, and the depositor can withdraw at par, which is a put option back to the bank.
cards.originalText: The bank models its retail non‑maturity deposits as floating‑rate, putable bonds.

cards.explanation: Mortgages show negative convexity when rates fall because prepayments accelerate, which shortens the life of the cash flows (contraction risk).

cards.statement: Spectral and distorted risk measures are not widely used in practice and are largely of academic interest.
cards.explanation: They are not intuitive, since a spectrum or distortion function must be chosen. VaR and expected shortfall are the most commonly used measures, and standard deviation remains a simple, familiar measure.

cards.statement: The copula approach to risk aggregation is characterized by great difficulty in validating the parameterization and in building the joint distribution.
cards.explanation: Copulas are flexible and capture nonlinear and higher-order dependence, but their parameterization is very hard to validate and building the joint distribution is very difficult.

cards.statement: Benchmarking a model against another model provides little comfort that the model actually reflects reality.
cards.explanation: Benchmarking compares one model or calibration with another, not with actual outcomes, so it only confirms broad comparability and says little about absolute levels or realism.
cards.originalText: Benchmarking.

cards.loText: Describe the recommendations by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) that supervisors should consider in order to make effective use of internal risk measures, such as economic capital, that are not designed for regulatory purposes.
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: The BIS recommendation on counterparty credit risk says banks should consider using additional methods, such as stress testing, to help cover all exposures.
cards.explanation: Counterparty credit risk measurement methods involve trade-offs and no single method covers every exposure, so they should be supplemented with complementary methods such as stress testing.
cards.originalText: Counterparty credit risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.loText: Describe the recommendations by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) that supervisors should consider in order to make effective use of internal risk measures, such as economic capital, that are not designed for regulatory purposes.
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: The BIS recommends that all risks should be directly quantified within the economic capital model.
cards.explanation: The BIS acknowledges that not all risks can be directly quantified. Material hard-to-quantify risks, such as funding liquidity and reputational risk, are captured through compensating controls such as sensitivity analysis, stress testing or scenario analysis.
cards.originalText: All risks should be directly quantified within the economic capital model.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.loText: Describe the recommendations by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) that supervisors should consider in order to make effective use of internal risk measures, such as economic capital, that are not designed for regulatory purposes.
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: A bank should be able to demonstrate how its economic capital model has been integrated into the business decision-making process.
cards.explanation: This follows the BIS recommendation on using internal risk measures to assess capital adequacy: the model must feed real business decisions, not just risk reporting.
cards.originalText: A bank should be able to demonstrate how its economic capital model has been integrated into the business decision‑making process.

cards.subject: Operational Risk

cards.loText: Describe the recommendations by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) that supervisors should consider in order to make effective use of internal risk measures, such as economic capital, that are not designed for regulatory purposes.
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: Economic capital model validation should be rigorous and comprehensive, aimed at demonstrating that the model is fit for purpose.
cards.explanation: Rigorous and comprehensive validation is one of the BIS recommendations for making effective use of internal risk measures.
cards.originalText: Economic capital model validation should be rigorous and comprehensive, aimed at demonstrating the model is fit for purpose.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.loText: Describe the recommendations by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) that supervisors should consider in order to make effective use of internal risk measures, such as economic capital, that are not designed for regulatory purposes.
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: An economic capital model helps guide key decisions, such as capital allocation, by assessing the difference between stand-alone and diversified risk.
cards.explanation: The BIS expects the model to be integrated into business decisions, and the board should understand the gap between gross (stand-alone) and net (diversified) risk.
cards.originalText: Our economic capital model helps guide key decisions, such as capital allocation, by assessing the difference between standalone and diversified risk.

cards.loText: Describe the recommendations by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) that supervisors should consider in order to make effective use of internal risk measures, such as economic capital, that are not designed for regulatory purposes.
cards.reading: ORR-19: Range of Practices and Issues in Economic Capital Frameworks
cards.statement: A bank should assess whether the dependency structures in its credit portfolio model are appropriate and use supplementary approaches, such as sensitivity and scenario analysis, to address the model's limitations.
cards.explanation: This is the BIS recommendation on dependency modeling in credit risk: scrutinise the dependency structures and cover model limitations with sensitivity and scenario analysis.
cards.originalText: The bank assesses whether the dependency structures in its credit portfolio model are appropriate and uses supplementary approaches such as sensitivity and scenario analysis to address model limitations.
